items.title: Giant-Cell Arteritis.
items.abstract: Giant-cell arteritis is a granulomatous vasculitis of large and medium-sized arteries that occurs almost exclusively in older adults. Suspected giant-cell arteritis warrants urgent diagnostic evaluation and, when ischemic risk is high, immediate treatment before diagnostic confirmation. Although glucocorticoids remain the cornerstone of therapy, treatment is frequently prolonged, associated with substantial toxic effects, and complicated by relapses. Advances in vascular imaging and insights into disease immunopathogenesis have expanded our understanding of disease heterogeneity and enabled the development of targeted therapies, particularly interleukin-6-receptor and Janus kinase inhibitors. Here, we review current concepts in the pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnosis, and management of giant-cell arteritis and highlight areas of uncertainty that warrant further investigation.

items.title: Silent disabilities in Takayasu arteritis: the overlooked burden of functional decline.
items.abstract: Takayasu arteritis (TAK) is associated with a multidimensional burden that may not be adequately reflected by conventional inflammatory or vascular assessments. Functional performance, fatigue, physical activity, sleep, and quality of life (QoL) may capture complementary aspects of disease impact. To characterize objective functional performance and patient-reported burden in adults with TAK and explore associations of functional performance with disease activity, angiographic extent, treatment exposure, and clinical characteristics. This cross-sectional study included 32 adults with TAK. Functional performance was assessed using the 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT) and Sit-to-Stand (STS) test; patient-reported outcomes using SF-36, Fatigue Severity Scale, International Physical Activity Questionnaire, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Disease activity was assessed using ITAS-2010. The mean age was 47.9 ± 12.9 years, and 87.5% were female. Active disease was present in 65.6% of patients, and 59.4% were receiving corticosteroids. Low physical activity levels were observed in 71.9% of participants. Higher prednisone dose correlated negatively with STS performance (r = -0.404, p = 0.030). BMI was inversely associated with 6MWT distance (r = -0.420, p = 0.021) and positively correlated with fatigue severity (r = 0.515, p = 0.004). Patients with angiographic Type 5 disease exhibited significantly poorer STS performance and shorter 6MWT distances than those with Type 2 a (p = 0.013 and p = 0.041). Active TAK was also associated with fewer STS repetitions (p = 0.042). Objective functional performance was associated with prednisone dose, BMI, angiographic extent, and disease activity. The 6MWT and STS test may complement conventional TAK assessments; longitudinal studies are needed to establish their clinical and prognostic utility.

items.title: Extended MRI versus routine and expert ultrasound in suspected giant cell arteritis: a prospective head-to-head study.
items.abstract: Imaging is central to diagnosing giant cell arteritis (GCA). Ultrasound (US) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are widely used, but prospective head-to-head comparisons are limited. To compare extended MRI with routine US for suspected giant cell arteritis and to assess the influence of US expertise. Ninety-three consecutive patients with suspected GCA underwent US and MRI (median interval 0 days). US assessed the superficial temporal, carotid, subclavian and axillary arteries. MRI additionally evaluated the superficial occipital and vertebral arteries, the thoracic and suprarenal abdominal aorta, and the abdominal aorta. MRI was analyzed (1) restricted to the same vessels as US and (2) including all MRI-assessed vessels (MRI-all). Readers were blinded to clinical data. The reference standard was the final clinical diagnosis after 12 weeks. GCA was confirmed in 45/93 patients. MRI-all vessels showed higher sensitivity than routine US (80% vs. 44%, p < 0.001), with similar specificity (96% vs. 94%). MRI restricted to US-matched vessels also showed higher sensitivity (60% vs. 44%, p = 0.04). Expert US detected 12/15 cases (80%). MRI identified vasculitis in non-US-accessible territories in 9/45 patients (20%). Predictive values reflected the prevalence of the enriched fast-track. Extended MRI was more sensitive than routine US in this fast-track cohort, whereas expert US achieved comparable sensitivity. Ultrasound remains appropriate when expertise is available; MRI is useful for atypical, large-vessel, or inconclusive cases. Question In suspected giant cell arteritis, the diagnostic impact of extended MRI versus routine ultrasound, and the role of ultrasound expertise, remain uncertain. Findings Extended MRI had higher sensitivity than routine ultrasound, but expert ultrasound reached comparable sensitivity; both modalities maintained high overall specificity. Clinical relevance Ultrasound should remain the first line when local expertise is available, while MRI can support atypical, large-vessel, or inconclusive cases.

items.title: Elucidating the molecular interplay between nicotine and ankylosing spondylitis: an integrated systems toxicology study.
items.abstract: This study aims to investigate the potential effects and underlying mechanisms of nicotine on ankylosing spondylitis(AS). Potential targets of nicotine were predicted using the CTD. Gene targets for AS were retrieved from four public databases. Protein-protein interaction network and pathway enrichment analysis were performed. Subsequently, we constructed seven machine learning models using the GSE73754 dataset to identify diagnostic biomarkers. Molecular docking was performed to predict binding affinities and modes, complemented by molecular dynamics simulations for detailed interactions and conformational changes. Lastly, we conducted an in silico knockout experiment using the GSE232131 dataset for validation. After systematic screening of multiple databases, we identified 38 overlapping targets between nicotine and AS. Network analysis refined these to eight hub targets. Enrichment analysis highlighted their significant involvement in inflammatory and immune-related processes, particularly the IL-17 and NF-κB signaling pathway. The logistic regression model exhibited the best predictive performance (AUC 0.905). Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations revealed stable binding complexes, especially with TNF, IL1B and IL10. A virtual knockout experiment revealed TNF as a critical gene within the interaction network. This study provides computational evidence on nicotine's potential impact on AS development. It establishes a foundation for further research on AS preventive and therapeutic strategies. Moreover, the reproducible computational pipeline established can be readily adapted to investigate other environmental triggers in autoimmune diseases and inform the development of evidence-based public health policies related to nicotine exposure.

items.title: Volumetric fat fraction quantification of the sacroiliac joint: changes in axial spondyloarthritis.
items.abstract: To investigate the changes of fat fraction in the sacroiliac joint in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA), including both the cartilaginous joint and the posterior ligamentous joint (PSIJ), by using a volumetric analyzing method on proton-density fat fraction (PDFF) maps. Patients aged 18-45 years with low back pain that underwent a 3.0 T MRI scan of the sacroiliac joint with additional PDFF maps were retrospectively included. Semi-automatic segmentation of the subcortical region and the PSIJ was performed. Volumetric fat fraction parameters were quantified including histographic analysis. Comparison between axSpA and non-SpA patients was performed. Ninety-three patients including 44 axSpA and 49 non-SpA patients were included. Patients with axSpA had higher mean sacrum PDFF (58.2% vs. 52.5%, p = 0.004). The percentage of bone volume with PDFF ranged from 75% to 100% (i.e. PDFF75100) increased (24.0% vs. 8.9%, p < 0.001), while the percentages of PDFF2550 and PDFF5075 decreased (26.6% vs. 35.6%, p = 0.005, 33.7% vs. 42.0%, p < 0.001). The mean ilium PDFF was not different between groups (p = 0.284), while the percentage of PDFF5075 decreased (39.0% vs. 46.3%, p = 0.033) and the percentage of PDFF75100 increased (20.6% vs.10.6%, p = 0.008). Fat fraction of the PSIJ was not changed in axSpA. The results remained unchanged after correction of age, sex and BMI. By using a volumetric segmentation method, fat fraction of the cartilaginous sacroiliac joint was changed in axSpA while not the PSIJ. Changes of the fat fraction of both the cartilaginous and ligamentous sacroiliac joint was described in detail using a semi-automatic segmentation method.

items.title: Impact of testing method and analyte on the diagnosis of antiphospholipid syndrome: a survey by the association of medical laboratory immunologists.
items.abstract: To evaluate and compare the performance, variation, and agreement of ELISA and non-ELISA methods for detecting anti-cardiolipin (aCL) and anti-beta 2 glycoprotein 1 (aβ 2 GP1) antibodies across clinical laboratories and assess diagnostic standardization. ELISA and non-ELISA methods for IgG, IgM, and IgA aCL and aβ 2 GP1 antibodies were evaluated in patients with antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), APS-like disease, and healthy controls. Agreement (κ and Spearman correlation), sensitivity, specificity, area under the curve (AUC), and relative risk (RR) for APS, thrombotic events (TE), and pregnancy-related morbidity (PRM) were assessed. Correlations were generally stronger within ELISA and within non-ELISA than between ELISA and non-ELISA methods, although substantial inter-assay variability existed within both groups. For APS diagnosis, IgG aCL non-ELISAs demonstrated higher sensitivity than ELISAs (0.73-0.80 vs. 0.50-0.63; p=0.026) with similar specificity (0.96-0.99 vs. 0.94-1.00). AUCs for IgG aCL and IgG aβ 2 GP1 were comparable across individual assays regardless of method (0.83-0.93 and 0.76-0.94, respectively). Non-ELISA IgG aCL assays also showed higher RR estimates for APS (8.3-12.0 vs. 5.7-7.4; p=0.024). However, when aCL and aβ 2 GP1 results were assessed as a complete antibody profile, sensitivity, specificity, AUC, and RR did not differ significantly between ELISA and non-ELISA methods. Generally, the non-ELISAs showed better performance for selected analytes, particularly aCL IgG, while ELISAs demonstrated greater consistency. Although agreement between methods varied for specific antiphospholipid antibodies, overall diagnostic accuracy was comparable when the complete antiphospholipid antibody profile was assessed. Clinicians should consider these factors to ensure accurate and reliable diagnostics.

items.title: Osteopontin and organ damage in systemic lupus erythematosus: A cross-sectional study in Mexican patients.
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the relationship between circulating osteopontin (OPN) and irreversible organ damage in Mexican adults with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and to explore its relationship with disease activity, serological activity, and lupus low disease activity state (LLDAS).MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional study in consecutive adult patients with SLE from a Mexican tertiary referral centre. Demographic and clinical data were recorded at a single visit. Disease activity was assessed with the SLE Disease Activity Index 2000 (SLEDAI-2K) and irreversible damage with the SLICC/ACR Damage Index (SDI). LLDAS was defined according to published criteria. Plasma OPN concentrations were measured by ELISA. Patients were categorised as having no damage (SDI = 0) or any damage (SDI ≥1).ResultsSeventy-seven patients were included; mean age was 49.8 years (SD 12.9), 75 (97.4%) were women, and median disease duration was 20.0 years (IQR 16.0-25.0). Fifty patients (64.9%) had SDI = 0 and 27 (35.1%) had SDI ≥ 1 (median SDI among damaged patients 1.0, IQR 1.0-2.0). Overall disease activity was low (median SLEDAI-2K 0.0, IQR 0.0-2.0). Median plasma OPN was 15.18 ng/mL (IQR 8.20-52.58). Patients with damage had higher OPN than those without damage (36.23 ng/mL [IQR 11.73-83.62] vs 12.02 ng/mL [IQR 7.77-39.23]; p = 0.017). OPN correlated modestly with SDI total score (ρ = 0.25, p = 0.03). Disease activity was low and showed limited variability (median SLEDAI-2K 0.0, IQR 0.0-2.0), precluding a meaningful assessment of the association between OPN and disease activity.ConclusionsIn this cohort of Mexican adults with long-standing, predominantly quiescent SLE, higher circulating OPN concentrations were observed in patients with irreversible organ damage in unadjusted analyses. The limited variability in disease activity precluded a meaningful assessment of its association with OPN.

items.title: Racial Disparities in Lupus Nephritis: A Nationwide Analysis.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) disproportionately affects racial minorities and is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. National-level data on racial disparities in LN remains limited and our study aims to highlight key racial disparities and predictors of inpatient mortality in LN. Cross-sectional observational study. Discharge-level data from US hospitalizations included in National Inpatient Sample database. Adult hospitalizations with a primary/secondary diagnosis of LN were included from National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 to 2019 using ICD-10 codes and divided into African Americans (AA) or Hispanics versus other races. Not applicable. This was an observational analysis. Several variables, including demographics, outcomes, and health care burden were compared. Multivariate logistic regression was conducted for predictors of mortality. p value of ≤0.05 was considered significant. Among 104, 865 adult LN hospitalizations, 66.3% were AA or Hispanics. Compared with other races, this group were more often females (85.5% vs. 79.9%), younger (38.4 vs. 45.6 y), from lowest-income quartile (45.8% vs. 23.6%), and had Medicaid (30.6% vs. 19.4%). They also had higher rates of acute kidney injury/chronic kidney disease (AKI/CKD) (82.5% vs. 79.1%), ESRD (44.6% vs. 33.9%), and leaving against medical advice (3.0% vs. 1.7%), but lower rates of renal transplant (4.3% vs. 5.2%), transfers to skilled nursing facilities (8.7% vs. 13.3%), and mortality (1.7% vs. 2.6%). Significant mortality predictors included: age, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), Medicaid, small bed size, sepsis, pulmonary embolism/deep vein thrombosis (PE/DVT), and CKD. (All p≤0.05 unless specified). Review of medical data from an administrative database involved reliance on diagnostic coding, limited detailed clinical information, and residual confounding. African Americans and Hispanics represented two-thirds of LN hospitalizations and had distinct demographic profiles, reflecting greater socioeconomic disadvantage and renal disease burden. Mortality was influenced by age, comorbidity burden, Medicaid status, hospital size, sepsis, PE/DVT, and CKD highlighting key factors influencing potential disparities.

items.title: Glucocorticoid discontinuation and flare risk in remitted systemic lupus erythematosus: a propensity score-matched cohort study.
items.abstract: To assess flare risk during remission in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) patients comparing low-dose glucocorticoid (GC) maintenance and its discontinuation. Prospective data of SLE patients were retrospectively evaluated. Remission was defined as clinical-SLEDAI-2K=0 on prednisone (PDN) dose ≤5 mg/day and stable background therapy, flares as any increase in clinical-SLEDAI-2K>0 or escalation in SLE medications. Patients withdrawing GC (off-GC) during remission were compared with patients on PDN≤5 mg/day (on-GC) through propensity score matching (PSM). Time-varying exposure Cox regression and Simon-Makuch curve assessed flare predictors and flare-free remission. Among 541 patients, 480 achieved remission and 358 (74.6%) discontinued GC. 86 flares occurred: 48 in off-GC (2.07 flare/100 patients-year) and 38 in on-GC patients (3.44 flares/100 patients-year, 1.66 on/off-GC ratio). Flare-free survival (p = 0.189) and flare hazard (HR 0.727, 95%CI 0.450-1.172, p = 0.19) were similar in off and on-GC patients; results were confirmed after adjustment for baseline covariates (HR 0.673, 0.401-1.128, p = 0.1326). Skin rash (HR 1.997, 1.061-3.76, p = 0.032), arthritis/myositis (HR 2.827, 1.103-7.246, p = 0.03), leukopenia (HR 1.852, 1.004-3.415, p = 0.048), and vasculitis (HR 3.521, 1.691-7.33, p < 0.001) were associated with flare in off-GC patients. In PSM cohort (314 off-GC and 114 on-GC patients), no significant increase in flare rate was found during remission after GC discontinuation (HR 0.767, 0.386-1.524, p = 0.45). Flare occurrence in off-GC patients was not associated with damage accrual (IRR 1.598, 95%CI 0.746-3.424, p = 0.227). Glucocorticoid withdrawal was not associated with an increased flare hazard in SLE patients compared to low-dose maintenance.

items.title: Association of self-reported long-term or recurrent childhood antibiotic use and axial spondyloarthritis among HLA-B27-positive individuals.
items.abstract: To examine whether self-reported long-term or recurrent antibiotic use during childhood or adolescence is associated with axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) diagnosis among HLA-B27-positive individuals. We studied HLA-B27-positive adults of White European ancestry in UK Biobank who reported long-term/recurrent (≥3 courses/year) antibiotics during childhood/adolescence. AxSpA was ascertained from linked hospital, death and primary care records. Logistic regression estimated age- and sex-adjusted odds ratios (ORs). We assessed robustness using sensitivity analyses, positive and negative control outcomes (anterior uveitis and rheumatoid arthritis), quantitative bias analysis for differential recall, and construct validation in linked primary care data. Among 10,528 HLA-B27-positive participants, 206 had axSpA and 1,481 reported long-term/recurrent childhood/adolescent antibiotic use. Childhood exposure was associated with two-fold higher odds of axSpA diagnosis than none (OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.42-2.89; p < 0.001), with consistent estimates across sensitivity analyses. Associations with control-outcome were OR 1.80 (1.07-3.03) for anterior uveitis and 1.29 (0.87-1.91) for rheumatoid arthritis. In a separate construct-validation cohort of 57,627 participants with linked primary care data, self-reported childhood exposure identified a persistent high-antibiotic-use phenotype, with higher later-life prescription rates (adjusted incidence rate ratio 1.75, 95% CI 1.42-2.14) and exposure duration (2.14, 1.59-2.88); higher prescribing persisted after accounting for infection episodes. Under differential-recall assumptions, the median bias-adjusted OR was 1.72 (95% simulation interval 1.08-2.72) but adverse stress test attenuated OR to 1.42 (0.69-2.61). Self-reported early-life long-term/recurrent antibiotic use was associated with two-fold higher odds of axSpA among HLA-B27-positive individuals. Future research should examine antibiotic versus infection effects and potential microbiome mediation.

items.title: Isolated pulmonary Capillaritis presenting as massive Hemoptysis: a rare pulmonary manifestation of rheumatoid arthritis in a young female.
items.abstract: Pulmonary manifestations of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) most commonly include interstitial lung disease, pleural effusions, and rheumatoid nodules. Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH) due to isolated pulmonary capillaritis is an exceptionally rare and potentially fatal presentation, particularly in young adults with high serology-positive articular disease. A 27-year-old female with a known history of rheumatoid arthritis, hyperlipidemia, carpal tunnel syndrome and hyperthyroidism presented to the emergency department with acute chest pain, progressive shortness of breath, and massive hemoptysis. She developed hypoxemic respiratory failure requiring intensive care unit admission. On presentation, her blood pressure was 100/70 mmHg, heart rate 111 beats per minute, and respiratory rate 19 breaths per minute. Chest computed tomography (CT) revealed bilateral diffuse ground-glass opacities consistent with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH). Bronchoscopy with sequential bronchoalveolar lavage confirmed ongoing alveolar hemorrhage. Infectious studies were negative. Serologic evaluation for systemic vasculitis, including ANCA-associated vasculitis and anti-glomerular basement membrane disease, was unremarkable. Autoimmune testing demonstrated markedly elevated rheumatoid factor, ESR, CRP and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibodies. Given persistent diagnostic uncertainty, a surgical lung biopsy was performed and demonstrated isolated pulmonary capillaritis without granulomatous inflammation or immune complex deposition. A diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis-associated pulmonary capillaritis presenting as DAH was established. The patient was treated with pulse-dose intravenous corticosteroids followed by additional immunosuppressive therapy of rituxumab, resulting in rapid clinical and radiographic improvement. A repeat chest CT performed one month after initiation of corticosteroid and rituxumab therapy showed significant resolution of the previously noted ground-glass opacities. Isolated pulmonary capillaritis due to rheumatoid arthritis should be considered in cases of unexplained massive hemoptysis. Although rare, rheumatoid arthritis (RA) can present with life-threatening pulmonary hemorrhage, highlighting the need for early multidisciplinary evaluation and prompt initiation of immunosuppressive therapy.

items.title: [Expert consensus on blood pressure and vascular assessment and multidisciplinary management of adult Takayasu arteritis (2026 edition)].
items.abstract: Takayasu arteritis-related hypertension (TARH) is common and often refractory, leading to severe target organ damage involving the heart, brain, kidneys, and major vessels, which significantly impacts patient prognosis and is a major cause of death in patients with Takayasu arteritis. However, there is currently no unified consensus on systematic evaluation and standardized management in clinical practice. To address this, the Zhongshan Hospital of Fudan University took the lead, in collaboration with the Rheumatology Branch of Chinese Women's Medical Association, Rheumatism Committee of Chinese Association of Integrative Medicine, Rheumatology Branch of Shanghai Medical Association, and multidisciplinary experts from across China. On the basis of the "Chinese multidisciplinary recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of Takayasu's arteritis-related hypertension" published in 2021, this consensus has been updated to address key issues in TARH, including epidemiology, definition, early identification and comprehensive assessment of high-risk populations, antihypertensive drug therapy, and revascularization, with 16 core clinical questions identified. Through evidence retrieval and multiple rounds of discussion and voting, 28 recommendations have been formulated. items.title: From Disease Susceptibility to Prognosis in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus-Associated Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Background: Systemic lupus erythematosus-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension (SLE-PAH) is a severe complication requiring early recognition and risk stratification. However, factors associated with prevalent disease, non-invasive detection, incident PAH, and prognosis after diagnosis are frequently conflated. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were initially searched through 23 September 2026, and searches of all four databases were updated on 1 November 2026. Observational evidence was evaluated using a structured clinical-pathway framework and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and findings were synthesized narratively because of clinical and methodological heterogeneity and potentially overlapping cohorts. Results: Thirty-five studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Serositis, interstitial lung disease, pericardial effusion, anti-U1 RNP and anti-Ro/SSA antibodies, reduced diffusing capacity, and microvascular abnormalities were mainly associated with prevalent or concomitant disease. Non-invasive detection was supported by a multimodal approach incorporating symptoms, biomarkers, pulmonary function, and echocardiography, with right heart catheterization required for PAH confirmation. Evidence on incident, catheterization-confirmed PAH prediction was limited. After diagnosis, functional class, exercise capacity, pulmonary vascular load, right-heart function, and serial risk status were recurrent prognostic indicators. Conclusions: Evidence is more extensive for prognosis after established SLE-PAH than for incident prediction, highlighting the need for externally validated SLE-specific screening and risk-stratification tools.

items.title: Redox Control of Mesenchymal Stromal Cell-Mediated Immunoregulation in Rheumatoid Arthritis: From Licensing to Stromal Inflammaging.
items.abstract: Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) are dynamic regulators of the immune response whose immunomodulatory functions are influenced by inflammatory cues. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), acute inflammatory signals enhance MSC function through licensing, whereas chronic exposure to the inflammatory microenvironment promotes mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, senescence, and loss of immunoregulatory capacity. In parallel, fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) undergo metabolic and mitochondrial reprogramming that promote inflammatory activation, apoptosis resistance, and tissue-destructive behavior. This structured narrative review examined the literature on MSC licensing and T-cell regulation in rheumatoid arthritis. A comprehensive literature search of ScienceDirect, Web of Science, and PubMed was conducted in September and November 2026 to identify relevant studies published between 1990 to 2026. Search terms included combinations of "mesenchymal stem/stromal cells", "T-cells", "rheumatoid arthritis", "RA", "priming/licensing", "immunomodulation", "mitochondrial dysfunction", "metabolic reprogramming", and "synovial environment". Original research articles and reviews were included. Of 273 initially identified articles, 182 remained after duplicate removal, and 125 were included in the final analysis. Studies were considered eligible if they addressed relevant information on MSC licensing, MSC immunomodulation, mitochondrial metabolism, or stromal-immune interactions in RA. Evidence from human-derived cells and experimental arthritis models was considered. Mechanistic studies in non-RA models were included where they provided relevant insights into the underlying mechanisms of MSC licensing and T-cell regulation. Studies were excluded if they lacked sufficient relevance to RA, did not provide original experimental data, or contained insufficient mechanistic information. Screening was performed by S.S. and J.D. and evaluation was conducted separately before comparison. Findings from human RA samples and experimental models suggest that inflammatory licensing can transiently enhance MSC-mediated immunosuppression through metabolic adaptation, whereas prolonged inflammation is associated with mitochondrial dysfunction, redox imbalance, and senescence. These changes may reduce the capacity of MSCs to suppress pathogenic T-cell responses. In parallel, RA-FLS exhibit altered glycolytic and lipid metabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction, and increased inflammatory and invasive behavior. These findings suggest that metabolic dysregulation may reinforce stromal-immune interactions that propagate synovitis; however, the precise mechanism has not been elucidated in RA patient-derived MSCs. This review provides an integrated framework linking inflammatory licensing, metabolic flexibility, mitochondrial homeostasis, and stromal-immune interactions to understand MSC immunoregulatory function in RA and the contribution of FLS to RA pathogenesis. Here, we highlighted processes contributing to persistent synovial inflammation and identified potential targets for therapeutic intervention. Strategies to preserve metabolic flexibility and mitochondrial homeostasis warrant further investigation, but mechanistic confirmation in human RA models and clinical studies is needed before potential therapies can be developed.

items.title: Impact of cardiovascular risk factors and atherosclerosis-related diseases on the OMERACT giant cell arteritis ultrasound score.
items.abstract: To evaluate the impact of cardiovascular risk (CVR) factors and atherosclerosis-related diseases on the OMERACT Giant Cell Arteritis Ultrasound Score (OGUS) in patients with suspected giant cell arteritis (GCA). This retrospective monocentric study included all patients undergoing temporal and axillary artery ultrasonography for suspected GCA between January 2022 and May 2025 in a fast-track clinic. CVR factors (systemic hypertension, diabetes, hypercholesterolaemia, smoking) and atherosclerosis-related diseases (coronary artery disease, peripheral arterial disease, ischaemic stroke, chronic kidney disease) were recorded. Intima-media thickness was measured and OGUS calculated. Associations between OGUS and cardiovascular variables were assessed in the whole population and in the GCA subgroup, using univariate and multivariate linear regression analyses. Among 152 patients, 72 met the 2022 ACR/EULAR classification criteria for GCA. OGUS and cranial OGUS were significantly higher in GCA than in non-GCA patients ( P  < 0.001). In the whole population, OGUS was higher in those with systemic hypertension and increased with age. In GCA patients, OGUS was higher in males and in those with hypercholesterolaemia, and was positively correlated with age. Multivariate analysis confirmed age as independent determinants of OGUS in this subgroup. OGUS was not associated with ischaemic complications of GCA, including ophthalmic events and inflammatory strokes. In the univariate analysis in GCA, OGUS was higher in male, with hypercholesterolemia and increased with age. In the multivariate analysis, age was still associated with higher OGUS. CVR factors should be considered when interpreting OGUS at diagnosis and during follow-up in clinical trials.

items.title: Association Between Anti-Ro52 Antibody Concentration and Documented Depression in Patients with Sjögren's Disease: A Retrospective Observational Study.
items.abstract: Background/Objectives : Depression is a clinically relevant neuropsychiatric manifestation of Sjögren's disease, although the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Autoimmune and neuroinflammatory processes, including the potential role of autoantibodies, may contribute to its development. This study aimed to investigate the association between anti-Ro antibodies, with particular emphasis on anti-Ro52, and the presence of depression in patients with Sjögren's disease and to explore whether quantitative anti-Ro52 antibody levels may provide patient-level information relevant to a more personalized assessment of neuropsychiatric manifestations. Methods : This retrospective, observational, cross-sectional study included 141 adult patients with Sjögren's disease treated at the University Hospital of Split between 2020 and 2023. Depression was defined as a documented diagnosis supported by psychiatric evaluation. The association between anti-Ro52 antibody concentration and depression was assessed using Firth's penalized logistic regression, adjusted for age and sex, with correction for multiple testing using the false discovery rate procedure. A sensitivity analysis was performed after restricting the analysis to patients with primary Sjögren's disease. Results : Depression was documented in 16/141 patients (11.3%). Anti-Ro52 concentrations were available for 111 patients, including 13 with depression. Higher anti-Ro52 concentrations were significantly associated with lower odds of depression. A one-standard-deviation increase in anti-Ro52 concentration was associated with 70% lower odds of depression (OR 0.30; 95% CI 0.12-0.61; p < 0.001). The association remained significant after multiple-testing correction (overall FDR-adjusted p = 0.046). The inverse association remained significant in the sensitivity analysis restricted to patients with primary Sjögren's disease (OR per 1-SD increase = 0.38; 95% CI 0.14-0.82; p = 0.013). Conclusions : Higher anti-Ro52 antibody concentrations were associated with lower odds of documented depression in patients with Sjögren's disease after adjustment for age and sex. These findings suggest that quantitative serological profiling may provide patient-level information relevant to a more personalized assessment of neuropsychiatric manifestations. However, prospective studies using standardized depression assessments are required to determine the clinical relevance and potential utility of anti-Ro52 levels in individualized patients.

items.title: ISG15+ CD4+ T cells are enriched in anti-MDA5 dermatomyositis and promote IL-1β production via LFA-1.
items.abstract: Anti-MDA5 dermatomyositis (DM) is characterised by high risk of rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (ILD) and a prominent type I interferon (IFN) signature. We aimed to delineate IFN-stimulated CD4+ T-cell subsets in anti-MDA5 DM and elucidate their pathogenic roles. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on skeletal muscle biopsies from anti-MDA5 DM (n=3), anti-synthetase syndrome (n=3) and healthy controls (n=3). CD4+ T-cell ISG15 expression was quantified by flow cytometry in peripheral blood from dermatomyositis cohorts (n=86), other inflammatory myopathies (n=35) and healthy controls (n=39), including paired pre-/post-treatment samples (n=10). Serum CCL19 was determined by ELISA. Mechanistic insights were gained through in vitro stimulation of CD4+ T cells with IFNβ or recombinant ISG15, and functional validation using LFA-1 blockade. Muscle single-cell profiling unveiled a unique ISG15+CD4+ T-cell cluster exclusively detected in anti-MDA5 DM, transcriptionally enriched for type I IFN and antiviral responses. In peripheral blood, CD4+ T-cell ISG15 geometric mean fluorescence intensity (gMFI) was significantly elevated across dermatomyositis cohorts compared with healthy controls and other myositis subtypes, peaking in anti-MDA5 DM. Notably, ISG15 gMFI diminished following immunosuppressive therapy and correlated with systemic inflammatory markers as well as biomarkers associated with ILD presence (ferritin and KL-6). Transcriptionally, this cluster displayed CCR7 enrichment; correspondingly, circulating CCR7+ CD4+ T cells and serum CCL19 concentrations were significantly increased in anti-MDA5 DM. Functionally, IFNβ stimulation recapitulated the ISG15, phenotype and triggered its secretion. Extracellular ISG15 potentiated IL-1β transcription and release from CD4+ T cells via LFA-1, as shown by blockade inhibition. ISG15+ CD4+ T cells constitute a treatment-responsive, IFN-driven pathogenic axis in anti-MDA5 DM, amplifying inflammation via ISG15-LFA-1-mediated IL-1β production. These findings identify a novel therapeutic target in this high-risk ILD complication.

items.title: Severe Progressive Multifocal Axonal Neuropathy After a Prolonged Fibrotic Interstitial Lung Disease Phase in MPO-ANCA-Associated Vasculitis: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Microscopic polyangiitis (MPA) is an antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated small-vessel vasculitis that may affect multiple organs. Interstitial lung disease (ILD), particularly with a usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern, may precede systemic vasculitis and delay diagnosis. We report a patient with initially undifferentiated fibrotic ILD identified in 2023, with radiological suspicion of UIP/IPF. The initial immunological evaluation in December 2023 was inconclusive: ANCA testing by indirect immunofluorescence was non-diagnostic, while antigen-specific MPO-ANCA and PR3-ANCA assays were negative. Over the following two years, the patient developed recurrent fever, progressive respiratory symptoms, systemic inflammation, anaemia, renal impairment, and severe bilateral lower limb weakness leading to loss of ambulation. Electroneurography demonstrated a severe, predominantly axonal sensorimotor neuropathy with multifocal involvement, while sural nerve biopsy revealed vascular inflammatory changes, raising the possibility of vasculitic neuropathy, although chronic thrombotic microangiopathy remained a possible coexisting process. In October 2025, markedly elevated MPO-ANCA levels were detected during evaluation of progressive multisystem disease. Whether this change reflected seroconversion during disease evolution or differences related to earlier testing cannot be determined retrospectively. The diagnosis of MPA was supported by the combination of markedly elevated myeloperoxidase (MPO)-ANCA levels, fibrotic ILD, renal dysfunction, systemic inflammation, severe multifocal neuropathy, and the nerve-biopsy findings. Treatment with high-dose corticosteroids, rituximab, intravenous immunoglobulin, and rehabilitation was followed by partial neurological recovery, although significant lower limb deficits persisted. This case illustrates the diagnostic challenges posed by severe MPO-ANCA-associated vasculitis following a prolonged fibrotic ILD phase. However, the available evidence does not establish whether the initial pulmonary fibrosis was an early manifestation of vasculitis or a coexisting fibrotic lung disease. The case also demonstrates that meaningful functional improvement may occur despite severe electrophysiological abnormalities.

items.title: Genetic Testing of Suspected Intestinal Behçet's Disease to Identify Monogenic Mimics.
items.abstract: Background: Intestinal Behçet's disease is difficult to distinguish from other immune-mediated inflammatory diseases of the gastrointestinal tract such as Crohn's disease. In recent studies, researchers have reported that multiple monogenic autoinflammatory diseases can mimic Behçet's disease, making differential diagnosis more challenging. We aim to retrospectively describe the clinical and laboratory features of six pediatric cases with suspected intestinal Behçet's disease and identify potential monogenic mimics. Methods: This study is a retrospective case series. All patients underwent specialized digestive system evaluation including symptomatology, laboratory examinations, imaging, endoscopy, and pathology. Whole-exome sequencing was conducted to identify potential monogenic mimics. Results: All patients presented with prominent inflammation in the ileocecal region. A likely pathogenic de novo variant in a gene ( RELA ) associated with a mimicking disease phenotype was identified in one out of six patients, while a second patient had a de novo variant of uncertain significance (VUS) in RELA . A VUS in TNFAIP3 gene was identified in a third patient but was inherited from an unaffected parent. The other three patients either had no detected variant (two cases), or a very likely benign coincidental variant (in CCR1 gene). Conclusions: Monogenic autoinflammatory disorders can be mistaken for Behçet's disease. We emphasize the importance of genetic testing in pediatric patients with intestinal Behçet's disease who present with atypical clinical symptoms, but also the importance of using tools to estimate the likelihood of variant pathogenicity, to avoid the overinterpretation of variant significance.

items.title: Recognizing treatment non-response in anti-MDA5-positive rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease: a trajectory-based framework for parallel escalation.
items.abstract: Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 antibody-positive dermatomyositis complicated by rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (anti-MDA5-positive RP-ILD) can progress from inflammatory lung injury to refractory respiratory failure within a short and clinically uncertain interval. Existing literature has largely evaluated individual immunomodulatory regimens, prognostic factors or organ-replacement outcomes, but provides limited guidance on when an inadequate early response should be regarded as clinically actionable treatment failure. This gap is important because persistent disease activity may coexist with infection, drug toxicity, pulmonary vascular events, air-leak syndromes and ventilation-related injury, each of which changes the expected benefit and risk of further immunosuppression. In this narrative review, we distinguish treatment non-response, treatment failure and refractory disease as related but non-equivalent concepts. We then organize evidence on treatment exposure, oxygenation and imaging trajectories, inflammatory activity, competing causes of deterioration, respiratory-support requirements and future treatment eligibility into a T0-T6 trajectory-based framework. The framework treats rescue immunomodulation, diagnostic reassessment, critical-care activation and preservation of advanced-support options as parallel decisions rather than consecutive treatment steps. It is intended as a structured communication and research model, not as a validated staging system or prescriptive clinical guideline. Its principal contribution is to define the questions that should be revisited when continued observation may threaten otherwise feasible treatment options.

items.title: Intestinal microbiota alterations link subclinical inflammation and clinical phenotypes in familial Mediterranean fever.
items.abstract: Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) is an autoinflammatory disease caused by mutations in the Mediterranean fever ( MEFV ) gene. Although FMF is classically associated with serosal inflammation, emerging evidence suggests intestinal involvement. We aimed to investigate subclinical intestinal inflammation in patients with FMF by assessing fecal calprotectin (FCP) levels and intestinal microbial and fecal metabolic profiles. Thirty patients with FMF from three hospitals were stratified into the FCP-high (>94 μg/g) and FCP-low (≤94 μg/g) groups. For intestinal microbiota analysis, patients with FMF were also compared with healthy controls and patients with inflammatory bowel disease unclassified (IBDU) from previous multicenter studies. Elevated FCP levels were detected in 26.7% patients. The FCP-high group had lower hemoglobin levels and a trend toward lower albumin levels. Compared with healthy controls, patients with FMF showed reduced alpha diversity and differences in overall microbiota composition. A higher relative abundance of Bifidobacterium longum and lower relative abundances of Faecalibacterium , Blautia , and Blautia obeum showed exploratory associations with arthritis, as well as lower albumin and hemoglobin levels. The FCP-high group showed greater depletion in the relative abundance of Blautia and nominally higher fecal 2-amino-2-methyl-1-propanol levels. The relative abundance of Lactobacillus , Streptococcus , and Enterococcus showed stepwise increased from healthy controls to the FCP-low FMF, FCP-high FMF, and IBDU with MEFV mutation groups, whereas that of Fusicatenibacter and Agathobacter showed stepwise decreased across these groups. This exploratory study identified associations among FMF, elevated FCP, and alterations in the intestinal microbiota. Elevated FCP in a subset of clinically remitted patients may suggest possible subclinical intestinal inflammatory activity.

items.title: Systemic lupus erythematosus and cutaneous manifestations: emerging treatment approaches.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic and complex autoimmune disease associated with significant morbidity and a relapsing-remitting course. Diagnosis and management remain challenging because of heterogeneous clinical presentations and variable treatment responses, reflecting the underlying immune dysregulation driving disease pathogenesis. Cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE) may occur as an isolated skin disorder or as part of the broader clinical spectrum of SLE. The skin is the second most frequently affected organ system in SLE. Cutaneous manifestations occur in 70%-85% of patients during the disease course and represent the initial presenting feature in up to one-quarter of patients. CLE can occur as a manifestation of SLE or independent of systemic disease. The clinical significance of cutaneous manifestations lies in their diagnostic value, prognostic associations with systemic disease activity, and therapeutic implications for patient management. Cutaneous manifestations frequently present early and can serve as the sole clue to SLE, helping establish diagnosis before systemic involvement. Certain lesions, such as acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus, vasculitis, and bullous lupus, correlate with systemic disease activity and severity, while others, such as discoid lupus erythematosus, may predict more localized disease but carry a risk of permanent scarring. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the spectrum of cutaneous manifestations of SLE, focusing on their underlying pathophysiology, diagnostic relevance, and current management approaches.

items.title: Case Report: Coronary artery involvement and nonvisualization of pulmonary artery branches first detected during follow-up of Takayasu arteritis.
items.abstract: Takayasu arteritis (TA) is a chronic granulomatous large-vessel vasculitis of unknown etiology that can involve the coronary and pulmonary arteries. A 30-year-old woman presented with crushing chest pain and was found to have 95% stenosis at the ostium of the left main coronary artery. Approximately 3.5 months after coronary stent implantation, severe in-stent restenosis occurred, requiring balloon angioplasty. Positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) showed thickening of the ascending aorta and aortic arch wall with increased fluorodeoxyglucose uptake, supporting the clinical diagnosis of TA. She received glucocorticoids and methotrexate and, because of persistent coronary disease, underwent off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting, followed by tocilizumab. During follow-up, C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate remained within reference ranges. In September 2025, echocardiography estimated a mean pulmonary artery pressure of 21 mmHg, whereas an October examination did not report pulmonary hypertension. On October 15, 2025, right heart catheterization measured a pulmonary artery pressure of 39/10 mmHg (mean 20 mmHg), which did not meet the current hemodynamic threshold for pulmonary hypertension. Pulmonary angiography showed nonvisualization of the right upper and middle lobar pulmonary artery branches. Because of the lack of baseline pulmonary vascular imaging or a complete evaluation of alternative causes, the onset and etiology of this finding remain uncertain. Normal acute-phase reactants during tocilizumab therapy should not be regarded as evidence of the absence of vascular disease, and angiographic nonvisualization alone cannot establish active vasculitic occlusion.

items.title: Cohort-aware single-cell analysis of PBMCs identifies an interferon program specific to primary Sjögren's syndrome and limited immune convergence with periodontitis.
items.abstract: Periodontitis (PD) and primary Sjögren's syndrome (pSS) are epidemiologically linked, and shared peripheral immune dysregulation has been proposed. Published comparisons rest on bulk transcriptomes or on tests that treat cells as replicates, and in public data disease is confounded with study. We reanalyzed four public single-cell RNA-seq cohorts of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs; two PD, two pSS) with the donor as the unit of inference and cases compared with same-cohort controls. After removal of eight duplicated samples, 48 donors (24 controls, 10 PD, 14 pSS) and 317,205 cells in 28 subsets were analyzed for composition, pseudobulk expression and consensus regulon activity. A finding was considered replicated when significant in the pooled model (false discovery rate <0.05) and in both cohorts of a disease; differences between the PD and pSS effects were tested directly. PD showed no replicated change in any layer, and its transcriptome-wide perturbation did not exceed the permutation null. pSS showed a type I interferon program across lineages: STAT1(+), STAT2(+), ETV7(+) and IRF7(+) accounted for 25 of 44 replicated regulon-subset pairs, their targets were the interferon-stimulated genes that dominated the replicated differentially expressed genes, and an interferon score separated pSS from PD (area under the ROC curve 0.90-0.95). In the larger pSS cohort, 93% of the PBMC interferon signal arose from higher expression within cells, not from composition. Naive/central memory CD4 + T cells were reduced in both pSS cohorts. Cross-disease concordance was weak but exceeded permutation nulls (regulons, rho = 0.38, P = 0.031; genes, rho = 0.13, P = 0.012) and had two components: fewer CD56dim NK cells and more cells of a mixed T-like/adaptive-like NK subset in all four cohorts, and lower expression of glucocorticoid- and stress-responsive genes in cases across lineages. With pooled controls, the same data yielded "shared" regulons that did not survive cohort-aware testing, and 39%-68% of regulon-subset pairs differed between the controls of the PD and pSS studies. The replicated peripheral immune change is specific to pSS; what the two diseases share is limited to a compositional shift in the NK lineage and a stress-response signature of uncertain origin.

items.title: Factors associated with fatigue in systemic lupus erythematosus: a cross-sectional structural equation modeling analysis of depressive symptoms as a potential mediator.
items.abstract: This study examined physiological, psychological, and environmental factors associated with fatigue in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and assessed whether depressive symptoms statistically mediated the relationships between these factors and fatigue. A convenience sample of 252 patients with SLE was recruited from the Department of Rheumatology and Immunology, Second Hospital of Hebei Medical University, between June 2023 and June 2024. Guided by the Theory of Unpleasant Symptoms (TOUS), candidate variables were classified into physiological (including disease activity on the SLEDAI-2K, anemia, biologic agent use, and sleep disturbance), psychological (anxiety and depressive symptoms), and environmental factors (including employment status and social support). Pain severity and other clinically recorded variables were entered as covariates. Validated measures included the Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS), Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and Social Support Rating Scale (SSRS). Univariate analyses, Spearman correlation analysis, and multivariable linear regression were performed using SPSS 26.0. Structural equation modeling (SEM) and indirect-effect testing based on bootstrapping (2,000 resamples; percentile 95% confidence intervals) were performed in R (lavaan). Sensitivity analyses (robust estimation, a Bollen-Stine bootstrap, and covariate-adjusted and alternative mediator models) were also performed. Social support, depressive symptoms, sleep disturbance, pain severity, biologic agent use, and employment status were found to be independently related to fatigue. Moreover, social support and sleep disturbance each had a significant indirect relationship with fatigue via depressive symptoms. The indirect associations persisted after clinical covariates were specified as predictors of both depressive symptoms and fatigue. However, social support was not independently associated with the binary fatigue outcome (FSS ≥ 4; OR = 0.96 per SD, P  = 0.837). In this cross-sectional sample, social support, depressive symptoms, sleep disturbance, pain severity, biologic agent use, and employment status were associated with fatigue, and depressive symptoms showed a statistically significant indirect association with fatigue through pathways linking social support and sleep disturbance. Because the data are cross-sectional, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory indirect associations that are compatible with, but do not establish, a mediating mechanism, and as hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of causality or treatment effect. Systematic assessment of social support and depressive symptoms, together with dynamic evaluation of sleep disturbance and pain, may inform comprehensive fatigue assessment, while longitudinal and interventional studies are needed before firm clinical recommendations can be made.

items.title: Shifting mortality profiles in rheumatoid arthritis in the United States, 1999-2024: a multiple-cause-of-death study.
items.abstract: Analyses restricted to rheumatoid arthritis (RA) as the underlying cause of death may incompletely characterize mortality involving RA. We examined population-based mortality trends and underlying-cause distributions among U.S. deaths mentioning RA. We conducted a repeated cross-sectional study using CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death data for 1999-2024. Deaths were classified as any mention of RA (RA-AM), RA as the underlying cause (RA-UCD), or RA recorded with another condition as the underlying cause (RA-nonUCD). Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were standardized to the 2000 U.S. population and expressed per million population. Trends were assessed using joinpoint regression. Among 244,813 deaths mentioning RA, 184,537 were RA-nonUCD. The RA-nonUCD proportion increased from 72.60% in 1999 to 82.03% in 2024. AAMRs declined from 36.67 to 23.16 for RA-AM, 10.07 to 4.13 for RA-UCD, and 26.62 to 19.01 for RA-nonUCD, with average annual percentage changes of -1.79%, -3.62%, and -1.39%, respectively. Among RA-nonUCD deaths, circulatory diseases remained the leading underlying cause, although their share declined from 46.75% to 30.05%. Within this category, the ischemic heart disease share decreased from 54.68% to 38.33%. The shares attributed to endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases, mental and behavioral disorders, and diseases of the nervous system increased from 4.47% to 7.77%, 1.38% to 4.72%, and 2.93% to 7.89%, respectively. Cancer and respiratory diseases ranked second and third by cumulative death counts. Population-based age-adjusted mortality rates involving RA declined during 1999-2024, with the largest relative decline observed when RA was the underlying cause. RA-nonUCD accounted for an increasing proportion of deaths mentioning RA. Within this group, circulatory diseases remained the leading underlying cause, while the proportions attributed to endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases, mental and behavioral disorders, and diseases of the nervous system increased.

items.title: 18 F-FDG PET/MRI and PET/CT for muscle and malignancy assessment in dermatomyositis.
items.abstract: Dermatomyositis (DM) requires advanced imaging to assess muscle inflammation and timely malignancy screening. Hybrid positron emission tomography (PET) imaging combines metabolic and anatomical data; however, whether it can comprehensively evaluate DM is unclear. We evaluated the ability of 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and PET/computed tomography (CT) to detect muscle involvement and cancer-associated myositis (CAM) in DM. This retrospective study evaluated 41 patients, including 39 with classic DM and 2 with clinically amyopathic DM (CADM), who underwent PET/MRI (n=27) or PET/CT (n=14). Whole-body MRI was scored for muscle edema, fatty infiltration and atrophy. FDG uptake was quantified using region-based maximum standardized uptake value (SUV max ) ratios (muscle-to-blood pool) and Deauville scores. Imaging parameters (edema scores, SUV max ratios, Deauville scores) and clinical data (muscle enzymes and myositis-specific autoantibodies) were analyzed. The sensitivity of PET/MRI was higher than that of PET/CT for detecting muscle involvement in classic DM (100% [25/25] vs. 78.6% [11/14]; P = 0.04). No muscle involvement was detected in CADM. Total edema scores correlated with creatine kinase (ρ=0.505, 95% CI 0.147-0.747; P<0.01) and lactate dehydrogenase (ρ=0.723, 95% CI 0.466-0.867; P<0.0001). Ten patients fulfilled the temporal definition of CAM (10/41, 24.4%), with nasopharyngeal carcinoma being the most common subtype (4/10, 40.0%). Stratified by modality, 2 malignancies were observed in the PET/MRI cohort (2/27, 7.4%), and 8 malignancies were identified in the PET/CT cohort (8/14, 57.1%). Anti-transcription intermediary factor-1γ antibody grade correlated with the SUV max ratio (ρ=0.452, 95% CI 0.168-0.667; P<0.01). PET/MRI detected muscle involvement more frequently than PET/CT in classic DM, while both PET/MRI and PET/CT contributed to malignancy assessment in this cohort. Hybrid PET imaging may aid disease phenotyping and cancer surveillance in DM.

items.title: Belimumab added to multi-target therapy in lupus nephritis: a retrospective cohort study of efficacy, divergent temporal response patterns, and safety.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is a severe complication of systemic lupus erythematosus. Belimumab, a B-cell-activating factor (BAFF) inhibitor, improves renal outcomes when added to standard therapy, but its efficacy and temporal effects when combined with multi-target therapy regimens containing tacrolimus remain poorly characterized. We compared multi-target therapy plus belimumab with multi-target therapy alone in active LN. In this retrospective cohort study, 28 patients with active LN (14 per group) received multi-target therapy (glucocorticoid, mycophenolate mofetil, and tacrolimus, a calcineurin inhibitor) with (case group) or without (control group) belimumab. The patients were assessed at baseline and 3, 6, and 12 months after treatment initiation. Primary endpoints were 24-hour urinary protein (24hUP), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR). C3, C4, anti-dsDNA, SLEDAI-2K, and IgG/IgA/IgM were the secondary endpoints. Comparisons were conducted using Welch's t or Mann-Whitney U tests (between-group), paired t or Wilcoxon tests (within-group), and Cohen's d effect sizes. Compared to baseline, both groups exhibited significant improvement in proteinuria, SLEDAI-2K, anti-dsDNA, and complement. eGFR remained stable, with no significant between-group differences at any timepoint. Temporal patterns diverged: the belimumab group showed earlier reduction in proteinuria (from 3 months) and IgG/IgA/IgM levels, whereas multi-target therapy alone showed earlier recovery of complement levels, with weak C4 recovery after treatment with belimumab. During twelve months of treatment, adverse events were infrequent and comparable between groups (all p  = 1.00). Both regimens substantially improved renal and serological outcomes over 12 months with an acceptable safety profile. Although the addition of belimumab did not significantly outperform multi-target therapy alone, the two regimens exhibited distinct, mechanistically coherent temporal signatures: inhibition of the BAFF pathway versus broad immunosuppression. These findings warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies.

items.title: The first two principal IL-1 receptor co-expression remodeling in allergic and autoimmune inflammation reveals disease-associated differences.
items.abstract: Interleukin-1 is a central mediator of inflammation, with its activity governed by the opposing functions of the signaling-competent receptor IL-1R1 and the inhibitory decoy receptor IL-1R2. However, comprehensive profiling of IL-1 receptor co-expression across immune cell subsets in diseases with distinct pathogenesis remains limited. We investigated the expression and co-expression patterns of IL-1R1 and IL-1R2 on twelve peripheral blood immune cell populations from patients with rheumatoid arthritis, patients with bronchial asthma, and healthy donors using multicolor flow cytometry. Receptor density was quantified as antibody-binding capacity per cell. Unsupervised clustering and logistic regression were applied to identify disease-associated candidate signatures and to develop exploratory diagnostic algorithms. Exploratory dimensionality reduction suggested separation of the three groups in this cohort, with each disease displaying a distinct IL-1 receptor remodeling pattern. Bronchial asthma was characterized by a global shift toward the double-negative phenotype across most populations, profound decoy receptor deficiency, and a striking predominance of the double-positive phenotype in naive T cells. Rheumatoid arthritis exhibited a less pronounced double-negative shift, selective loss of decoy receptor on monocytes, and mixed cytotoxic T cell profiles with preserved signaling-competent phenotypes. Logistic regression models incorporating three parameters for RA showed high discrimination in this case-control cohort, with apparent and cross-validated performance remaining robust for this disease. These findings indicate that allergic and autoimmune inflammation are associated with distinct, cell-subset-specific IL-1 receptor signatures consistent with their divergent immunopathogenesis. The identified receptor profiles may serve as candidate biomarkers and provide hypotheses for mechanistic studies of interleukin-1 pathway dysregulation in chronic inflammatory diseases. The model requires external validation before any clinical application.

items.title: Pyroptosis in systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis: evidence grading, cellular crosstalk, and translational priorities.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) links persistent immune dysregulation to heterogeneous tissue injury, but the mechanisms that localise damage remain incompletely resolved. Pyroptosis is a gasdermin-mediated, pore-forming process that can connect nucleic-acid sensing and inflammasome activation to mediator release and tissue-cell dysfunction. Here, we evaluate the SLE and lupus nephritis (LN) literature along two independent axes: mechanistic evidence for pathway licensing, inflammasome activation, gasdermin execution, or terminal lysis, and disease relevance across non-lupus models, lupus models, patient-derived cells, human renal tissue, and longitudinal cohorts. Four conclusions emerge. First, execution-level evidence is confined to a few nodes, including oxidised mitochondrial DNA-driven GSDMD oligomerisation, myeloid caspase-11/GSDMD signalling, and GSDME-mediated tubular epithelial injury; most reported lupus "pyroptosis axes" demonstrate licensing or inflammasome activation only. Second, the direction of GSDMD function remains unresolved: pharmacological inhibition ameliorates experimental lupus, whereas genetic deficiency worsens autoimmunity, renal and pulmonary inflammation, and myeloid calcium homeostasis. Third, the tubulointerstitial compartment carries the strongest executor-level causal evidence in the kidney, whereas glomerular studies offer broader regulatory hypotheses but weaker execution-level proof. Fourth, no current biomarker is execution-specific, and no intervention has demonstrated executor target engagement in patients. We therefore present immune-tissue crosstalk as an evidence-graded framework rather than a demonstrated end-to-end circuit and define the spatial, longitudinal, and lineage-specific studies needed for mechanism-guided translation.

items.title: Temporomandibular Joint Involvement in Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis: Can Clinical Examination and Panoramic Radiography Predict MRI Findings?
items.abstract: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) involvement is common in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) and may impair function and craniofacial growth. Although magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the preferred imaging modality, its routine use in children is limited by cost, examination time, and potential sedation requirements. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of clinical examination and panoramic radiography (OPG) compared with MRI. Seventy patients with JIA (52 females; mean age 13.4 ± 2.8 years) underwent standardized TMJ assessment, OPG, and non-contrast enhanced MRI. A composite clinical score (0-7) was calculated based on muscle and TMJ tenderness, mandibular deviation, reduced maximum mouth opening and joint clicking. A score ≥3 was considered positive. MRI served as the reference standard, with TMJ involvement defined primarily by structural or functional abnormalities. At least one clinical sign of TMJ involvement was observed in 41% of patients. MRI-detected TMJ involvement was significantly more frequent among patients with a clinical score ≥3 than among those with a score <3 (92.0% vs. 24.4%; p < 0.001). Clinical examination showed 67.6% sensitivity, 94.4% specificity, 92.0% positive predictive value (PPV), and 75.6% negative predictive value (NPV). OPG findings were positive in 85.3% of MRI-positive patients and negative in all MRI-negative patients ( p < 0.001), corresponding to 85.3% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 100% PPV, and 87.8% NPV. Clinical examination and OPG may help identify patients with a higher likelihood of MRI-detected TMJ involvement who may benefit from further MRI evaluation.

items.title: Bilateral Popliteal Artery Aneurysms as a Manifestation of Vascular Behçet Disease: A Case Report and Literature Review.
items.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance : Popliteal artery aneurysmal involvement is an uncommon arterial manifestation of Behçet disease, and bilateral disease with thrombotic complications is particularly rare. Management is challenging because urgent limb revascularization must be balanced against an inflammatory vasculopathy associated with recurrent arterial events and loss of graft patency. Case presentation: A 50-year-old man presented with Rutherford IIa acute right lower-limb ischemia caused by thrombosis and distal embolization from a 4.4 cm true fusiform distal femoral-to-popliteal aneurysm. Computed tomography angiography also demonstrated a 2.4 cm contralateral true fusiform aneurysm with mural thrombus. Catheter-directed thrombolysis and adjunctive endovascular treatment restored distal perfusion, followed by Viabahn covered-stent exclusion of the right aneurysm. The asymptomatic left aneurysm was electively excluded 5 months later. Within the following year, acute left stent-graft occlusion required endovascular salvage, while right in-stent restenosis was treated with drug-coated balloon angioplasty. Recurrent vascular events prompted rheumatological evaluation, and vascular Behçet disease was diagnosed in 2022, followed by corticosteroid and methotrexate therapy. During approximately 5 years of follow-up, both popliteal stent grafts eventually occluded; however, collateral perfusion preserved limb viability, with only mild intermittent claudication and no rest pain or tissue loss at the latest follow-up. Conclusions: Bilateral popliteal aneurysmal disease with thrombosis may lead to recognition of vascular Behçet disease. Endovascular exclusion can provide immediate limb salvage and aneurysm control, but recurrent thrombosis, restenosis, and late loss of patency remain possible. Long-term management should integrate inflammatory disease control with vascular surveillance while distinguishing anatomical graft failure from clinical limb outcome.

items.title: A Qualitative Study Exploring Foot Pain and Its Impact on Daily Function in Early Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease frequently associated with significant foot pain, even in early stages. This study aimed to explore how patients with early RA perceive foot pain and its impact on daily activities. Semi-structured interviews were developed based on the Spanish Foot Function Index (FFI-Sp) in 25 patients with RA of less than five years' duration. Four key themes emerged: (1) limitations in performing daily activities due to foot-related problems; (2) descriptions of pain, such as burning and throbbing sensations; (3) emotional responses, including frustration and sadness; and (4) perceived changes in mobility, balance, and muscle strength. Patients reported pain as influenced by both intrinsic disease mechanisms and external factors. These findings highlight the early and substantial impact of foot involvement in RA and support the need for multidisciplinary interventions-encompassing orthopaedic care, psychosocial support, and patient education-to improve functional outcomes and quality of life. V (Qualitative study).

items.title: Catastrophic in-stent thrombosis with antiphospholipid syndrome: a case report.
items.abstract: In-stent thrombosis despite morphologically optimal stents remains a diagnostic challenge. Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a rare cause that drives thrombosis via tissue factor-mediated coagulation-a pathway not addressed by dual antiplatelet therapy. A 51-year-old male with cardiovascular risk factors underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention for anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Ten days later, he developed refractory ventricular fibrillation requiring extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation with veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and intra-aortic balloon pump support. Emergency angiography confirmed complete in-stent thrombosis; intravascular ultrasound excluded a mechanical cause. The intensive care course revealed a triad of red flags: unexplained in-stent thrombosis, recurrent extracorporeal circuit clotting despite stepwise heparin escalation, and arterial and venous thrombosis on full anticoagulation. This prompted antiphospholipid antibody testing, which showed persistent moderate-to-high titre anti-cardiolipin IgM-a profile within the 'controversial' zone of the 2023 ACR/EULAR classification criteria. The patient was managed as APS with intensified triple therapy, later transitioning from heparin to a vitamin K antagonist, and was discharged on Day 27 with no events at 3-month follow-up. Antiphospholipid syndrome should be considered in unexplained in-stent thrombosis even when laboratory criteria are not strictly met. The triad of unexplained in-stent thrombosis, anticoagulation refractory circuit clotting, and incident venous thrombosis is a clinically actionable pattern warranting empiric APS-directed management.

items.title: Treatment-Associated Leukocyte-Trafficking Vascular Inflammation in Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Bibliometric and Multicohort Transcriptomic Analysis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) synovitis involves vascular remodeling and leukocyte entry. Research has largely focused on angiogenesis, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), and hypoxia. We examined how these themes have developed and whether vascular-related inflammatory gene expression is reproducible across patient synovial datasets. We mapped RA vascular and endothelial research in the Web of Science Core Collection and analyzed public human synovial transcriptomes. Five predefined modules were scored separately within each dataset. Disease effects were pooled across independent studies using restricted maximum likelihood random-effects models with modified Hartung-Knapp inference. We tested Module C after adjustment for Module E, an endothelial abundance proxy, and assessed its change in paired baseline and week-12 samples from patients receiving anti-tumor necrosis factor (TNF) treatment. The 1568 eligible publications from January 2010 to July 2026 showed sustained growth in the field. Angiogenesis, VEGF, and hypoxia remained central, while terminology describing endothelial heterogeneity became more frequent. Across three independent RA-versus-healthy studies, Module C, representing leukocyte recruitment and trafficking, had the largest pooled disease effect: Hedges g = 1.772, 95% CI: 0.889-2.655, p = 0.0131. items.title: Spinal Gout Presenting with Acute Paraplegia: A Case Report and Literature-Based Diagnostic Framework.
items.abstract: Background : Spinal gout is an uncommon manifestation of chronic hyperuricemia caused by the deposition of monosodium urate (MSU) crystals within axial skeletal structures. Although gout predominantly involves peripheral joints, axial deposition within the ligamentum flavum, facet joints, and epidural space can lead to spinal cord compression and severe neurological impairment. Because clinical and radiological features mimic spinal neoplasms, epidural abscesses, and degenerative disorders, diagnostic delays are common. Case Presentation : A 58-year-old man with an 8-year history of poorly controlled hyperuricemia and essential hypertension presented with progressive lower-limb weakness, severe thoracic back pain, lower-body numbness below the T10 dermatome, and acute urinary retention over two weeks. Neurological examination revealed flaccid paraplegia (Medical Research Council grade 0/5 in both lower extremities), complete loss of pinprick and light touch sensation below T10, absent deep tendon reflexes, and loss of anal sphincter tone, corresponding to American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) Impairment Scale Grade A. Serum uric acid was elevated at 9.5 mg/dL, alongside mildly elevated inflammatory markers. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a posterior extradural mass from T9 to T12 with severe cord compression centered at the T11-T12 level. Multi-sequence MRI demonstrated T1 iso/hypointensity, T2 heterogeneous hypointensity, thick peripheral rim enhancement on post-contrast T1-weighted sequences, and no restricted diffusion on DWI. Emergency decompressive laminectomy was performed, revealing a chalky white mass compressing the dural sac. Histopathological evaluation confirmed monosodium urate crystal deposits surrounded by granulomatous inflammation and multinucleated foreign-body giant cells. Postoperatively, the patient was initiated on treat-to-target urate-lowering therapy with allopurinol alongside short-term colchicine prophylaxis. At the 6-month follow-up, lower-limb motor strength recovered to grade 4/5, cutaneous sensation was restored, voluntary sphincter control was regained (ASIA Impairment Scale Grade D), and serum uric acid was normalized to 5.2 mg/dL. Conclusions : Spinal gout should be considered in the differential diagnosis of acute spinal cord compression, even in patients without active peripheral tophi. Prompt surgical decompression combined with long-term urate-lowering therapy is essential to facilitate neurological recovery and prevent disease recurrence.

items.title: Statin-related immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy: a case report.
items.abstract: While the safety profile of statins is generally considered as robust, they are known to be associated with a spectrum of muscle-related adverse effects, most of which are mild and reversible upon discontinuation of statins with some rare but serious exceptions. A 63-year-old Chinese gentleman presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness and markedly elevated creatine kinase levels after 2.5 years of atorvastatin therapy. The diagnosis of immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) was ascertained with muscle biopsy and positive autoantibody of anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase, and his condition responded to immunosuppressive therapy. IMNM is a rare but serious side effect related with statin use with delayed onset. With potential possibility of permanent disability, it is an important side effect that requires primary care doctors to maintain a high level of vigilance. The prompt recognition and immunosuppressive therapy is the key to avoid serious consequences.

items.title: Cannabidiol for chronic pain in rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis: a randomized, placebo-controlled trial with exploratory tetrahydrocannabinol add-on.
items.abstract: Persistent chronic pain remains a major unmet need in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and ankylosing spondylitis (AS), even when inflammatory disease activity is low. Evidence for cannabinoid-based treatment in inflammatory rheumatic disease is limited. We investigated the efficacy and safety of low-dose cannabidiol (CBD) for chronic pain in RA and AS and explored the effects of adjunctive tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) in non-responders. In this multicentre, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, 66 patients with RA or AS and persistent pain despite low inflammatory disease activity were randomized 1:1 to oral CBD or placebo for 12 weeks. The primary endpoint was a reduction of at least 20 points on the pain visual analogue scale (VAS) at week 12. After the blinded phase, non-responders entered a 12-week open-label phase: non-responders in the placebo group switched to CBD, while non-responders in the CBD group received add-on THC. Secondary outcomes included continuous pain VAS, sleep quality measured by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), cognitive performance assessed by the Trail Making Test (TMT) and Digit Symbol Substitution Test (DSST), disease activity measures, and safety. At week 12, the primary endpoint was achieved by 9/32 patients (28%) receiving placebo and 3/30 patients (10%) receiving low-dose CBD. Low-dose CBD did not demonstrate superior pain relief compared with placebo and was associated with poorer sleep quality, while no significant between-group differences were observed for cognitive outcomes or inflammatory markers. In the exploratory open-label phase, 9/23 patients (39%) receiving CBD plus THC achieved the predefined pain response criterion compared with 2/25 patients (8%) receiving CBD alone. The CBD + THC group also showed greater improvements in continuous pain VAS and sleep quality. Low-dose CBD did not yield meaningful pain relief. The addition of low-dose THC was associated with improvements in pain and sleep quality. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in blinded randomized controlled trials.
