items.title: Platform and adaptive trial designs for multidomain psoriatic arthritis: a conceptual framework.
items.abstract: Psoriatic arthritis is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease involving peripheral joints, axial skeleton, entheses, tendons, skin, and nails, and is associated with pain, fatigue, and impaired physical function. Although targeted therapies have expanded substantially, many patients do not reach remission or low disease activity. Conventional randomised controlled trials typically evaluate single agents in selected populations with fixed designs and limited outcome sets, and are therefore poorly suited to address comparative effectiveness, multidomain phenotypes, treatment sequencing, and precision medicine questions. Platform trials and adaptive designs, including multi-group multi-stage approaches, offer a flexible alternative, enabling assessment of multiple treatment strategies within a single master protocol. This type of study design allows prespecified discontinuation of futile groups, expansion of promising interventions, and enrichment of responsive subgroups. This Review examines how adaptive platform trials could be tailored to psoriatic arthritis, addressing phenotyping, endpoint selection, biomarker integration, ethical and regulatory challenges, and feasibility, and offers practical considerations for future trial design in this field.

items.title: Understanding inflammatory mechanisms and skeletal remodeling in rheumatoid arthritis-associated bone loss.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic inflammatory disease that disrupts the balance between bone resorption and formation, leading to focal erosions, periarticular bone loss, and systemic osteoporosis. Pro-inflammatory cytokine networks enhance osteoclast-mediated bone resorption while impairing osteoblast-mediated bone formation. Although controlling inflammation can limit further skeletal damage, restoring established bone loss remains challenging. In this Review, we discuss how inflammatory cytokine networks disrupt bone remodeling and examine the skeletal effects of cytokine-targeted therapies. We also consider anti-resorptive and bone-anabolic therapies, as well as emerging molecular and regenerative approaches aimed at preserving skeletal integrity and promoting bone repair.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of biologics or targeted synthetics for moderate-to-severe Sjögren disease: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Sjögren disease (SjD) is a chronic, systemic autoimmune disorder characterized by mucosal dryness, multi-organ involvement, and profoundly reduced quality of life. We employed a network meta-analysis (NMA) to synthesize current evidence and evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of biologic/targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (b/tsDMARDs) for moderate-to-severe SjD. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and ClinicalTrials.gov from database inception to January 9, 2026. The primary outcome was the change from baseline to week 24 in EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI) score. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2 tool. We performed a frequentist NMA to compare multiple regimens simultaneously, with placebo as the reference. Results are presented as mean differences or risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals. Confidence in the evidence was assessed using the Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis framework. The protocol was pre-registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261279431). Of 7493 records identified, 21 RCTs evaluating 18 b/tsDMARDs were included. At week 24, reductions in ESSDAI scores from baseline were significantly greater with telitacicept (80 and 160 mg), iscalimab (150 and 600 mg), remibrutinib (100 mg), low-dose interleukin-2 (1 million IU), and nipocalimab (15 mg/kg) than with placebo. For the EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Patient Reported Index, significantly greater reductions from baseline to week 24 were observed with telitacicept (80 and 160 mg) versus placebo. During short-term follow-up, no statistically significant differences in the risks of adverse events (AEs) or serious AEs were detected between b/tsDMARDs and placebo. This NMA synthesizes the available evidence on b/tsDMARDs for moderate-to-severe SjD to inform further research. Although some agents showed evidence of efficacy, reliance on a single trial for most interventions and uncertainty regarding transitivity warrant cautious interpretation of indirect comparisons. Head-to-head trials incorporating composite efficacy endpoints are needed to strengthen the comparative evidence. Long-term safety surveillance should focus on rare, delayed, and treatment-specific AEs.

items.title: From pathway to patient: Mapping the new wave of targeted therapies in systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a highly heterogeneous autoimmune disease associated with substantial morbidity despite advances in standard-of-care treatment. Although recently approved biologic therapies targeting B-cell survival and type I interferon signaling have improved outcomes, many patients continue to experience persistent disease activity, flares, excessive glucocorticoid exposure, and progressive organ damage. Increasing understanding of SLE immunopathogenesis has accelerated the development of targeted therapies aimed at key molecular pathways involved in innate and adaptive immune dysregulation. This narrative review summarizes emerging therapeutic strategies with the potential to reshape SLE management in the near future. Novel agents target multiple pathogenic mechanisms, including intracellular signaling pathways (deucravacitinib, upadacitinib, orelabrutinib), innate immune activation through Toll-like receptor 7/8 inhibition (enpatoran) lymphocyte trafficking (cenerimod), plasmacytoid dendritic cell-driven type I interferon responses via BDCA2 targeting (litifilimab), T-cell/B-cell costimulatory signaling (dapirolizumab pegol), and B-cell survival pathways through dual BLyS/APRIL blockade (telitacicept) or BAFF receptor inhibition and B-cell depletion (obinutuzumab, ianalumab). Across phase 2 and phase 3 clinical trials, several of these agents have demonstrated meaningful improvements in disease activity, attainment of low disease activity states, glucocorticoid sparing, reduction of flares, and favorable effects on cutaneous, musculoskeletal, and renal manifestations, generally with acceptable safety profiles. The current therapeutic landscape is evolving from broad immunosuppression toward mechanism-based and precision medicine-guided treatment approaches. Ongoing phase 3 programs will determine the long-term efficacy, safety, and positioning of these agents within future treatment algorithms. Importantly, beyond achieving disease control and preventing flares, newer clinical trials increasingly incorporate GC tapering and minimization strategies as key therapeutic objectives. Collectively, these emerging therapies offer the prospect of individualized SLE management, with the potential to further improve long-term outcomes and reduce irreversible organ damage.

items.title: Headache in juvenile idiopathic arthritis: more common and phenotypically different than expected.
items.abstract: Headache is among the most common neurological complaints in childhood and can substantially impair quality of life. Although children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) experience chronic inflammation and recurrent pain, the prevalence and phenotype of primary headache in this population remain insufficiently studied. This cross-sectional case-control study was conducted in a tertiary pediatric rheumatology clinic between October and December 2025. A total of 109 children with JIA and 125 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) were included. Headache was assessed by structured questionnaire and neurological examination, and all diagnoses were established by a pediatric neurologist according to the International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition. Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for age, sex, family history of migraine, perceived sleep insufficiency and body mass index. The excess was confined to tension-type headache (TTH; 22.9% vs. 4.8%, p < 0.001), whereas migraine was equally frequent (14.7% vs. 12.8%, p = 0.71). After adjustment, JIA remained associated with TTH (odds ratio [OR] 6.94, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.62-18.39) but not with migraine (OR 1.81, 95% CI 0.79-4.13). Conversely, family history of migraine (OR 2.35, 95% CI 1.06-5.19) and perceived sleep insufficiency (OR 3.99, 95% CI 1.76-9.02) were associated with migraine but not TTH. No disease-related or treatment-related variable was associated with headache. Children with JIA show a selective excess of TTH rather than a uniform increase in primary headache, while established risk factors track with migraine. Systematic headache enquiry may improve recognition of this underrecognized comorbidity.

items.title: Anti-FcRn-mIL-2 fusion protein restores immune homeostasis by reducing pathogenic plasma cells in lupus nephritis.
items.abstract: The short half-life of interleukin-2 (IL-2) and its role in broad immune-cell activation limit its therapeutic use in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). We developed Anti-FcRn-mIL-2, a bifunctional fusion protein linking a receptor-biased IL-2 mutein to a monoclonal antibody against the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), to combine cellular immune regulation with IgG homeostasis modulation. Compared with wild-type IL-2, Anti-FcRn-mIL-2 exhibited greater thermal and plasma stability. In mice, it had a longer apparent half-life after subcutaneous administration and generated stronger renal fluorescence signals when labelled. In murine assays, Anti-FcRn-mIL-2 induced less conventional T-cell activation than wild-type IL-2. In peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from patients with SLE, treatment with Anti-FcRn-mIL-2 reduced B-cell responses and plasma-cell frequencies. In MRL/lpr mice, Anti-FcRn-mIL-2 treatment increased regulatory T-cell frequencies, reduced splenic plasma-cell frequencies, and lowered circulating IgG and anti-double-stranded DNA antibody levels. It also reduced renal IgG and complement C3 deposition and alleviated both proteinuria and renal histological injury. Under the regimens tested, Anti-FcRn-mIL-2 produced greater improvements in renal and humoral immune outcomes than coadministration of mIL-2 and Anti-FcRn. These findings demonstrate the immunomodulatory and IgG-lowering effects of Anti-FcRn-mIL-2 in MRL/lpr mice and support further preclinical evaluation for lupus nephritis.

items.title: Serologic stratification by anti-TRIM21/Ro52 and anti-TROVE2/Ro60 antibodies defines distinct longitudinal disease activity, patient-reported symptoms, and immunologic phenotypes in Sjögren's disease.
items.abstract: Anti-SSA/Ro antibodies are a hallmark of Sjögren's disease (SjD), but the respective roles of anti-TRIM21/Ro52 and anti-TROVE2/Ro60 antibodies remain unclear. We investigated whether distinct anti-TRIM21/Ro52 and/or anti-TROVE2/Ro60 serological profiles are associated with differences in clinical phenotype, systemic activity, patient-reported symptoms, and lymphoma risk over time. Patients from the prospective multicenter ASSESS cohort were stratified accordingly as Ro52-/Ro60-, Ro60+ only, Ro52+ only, or Ro52+/Ro60+. Baseline clinical, biological, and immunological parameters were compared across groups. Patient-reported symptoms (ESSPRI) and systemic disease activity (ESSDAI) were evaluated over 5 years using age-adjusted mixed-effects models. ESSDAI domains and lymphoma cases were also assessed. Among 365 patients, 123 were Ro52-/Ro60-, 25 Ro52+, 23 Ro60+, and 194 Ro52+/Ro60+. At baseline, both Ro52+ and Ro52+/Ro60+ patients displayed the highest levels of markers associated with systemic disease activity, including β2-microglobulin, positivity of rheumatoid factor and IFN-α levels. Conversely, Ro60+ patients resembled immunonegative patients. Baseline ESSPRI was higher in Ro52-/Ro60- compared with Ro52+/Ro60+ patients, but this difference faded over time, due to the ESSPRI worsening in Ro52+/Ro60+ patients. ESSDAI scores were consistently higher in Ro52+ and Ro52+/Ro60+ patients compared to other groups. Domain analysis indicated that biological, articular, hematological and glandular domains could contribute to these differences. Lymphoma events were recorded in 7/116 (6.0%) Ro52-/Ro60-, 5/24 Ro52+ (20.8%), 0/19 Ro60+, and 17/189 Ro52+/Ro60+ (9.0%) patients. Anti-TRIM21/Ro52 and anti-TROVE2/Ro60 are linked to distinct SjD phenotypes. Anti-TRIM21/Ro52 positivity is associated with greater systemic disease activity, whereas anti-TROVE2/Ro60, although useful for diagnosis, have a limited relationship with disease expression.

items.title: Therapeutic Plasma Exchange Use among ANCA-Associated Vasculitis Hospitalizations after PEXIVAS and Guidelines, 2016-2023.
items.abstract: Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) has historically been considered for antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) with severe kidney or pulmonary involvement. National inpatient use after publication of the Plasma Exchange in Vasculitis (PEXIVAS) trial remains incompletely characterized. We conducted a repeated cross-sectional analysis of adult National Inpatient Sample hospitalizations from 2016 through 2023. The primary AAV cohort used stable International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. We estimated survey-weighted annual and era-specific TPE use and age- and sex-adjusted era associations. Lupus nephritis (LN) served as a temporal comparator in an adjusted cohort-by-era model. Sensitivity analyses examined principal-diagnosis AAV, AKI, AKI requiring acute kidney replacement therapy (AKI-D), coded pulmonary hemorrhage, and length of stay greater than 1 day. The cohort included 20,866 AAV hospitalizations and 623 TPE events. Weighted TPE use declined from 4% in 2016-2019 to 2% in 2022-2023; the adjusted later-versus-baseline odds ratio (OR) was 0.49 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.39-0.62). Standardized TPE probabilities declined from 3.81% to 1.91% for AAV and from 1.04% to 0.68% for LN. The absolute difference-in-changes was -1.54 percentage points (95% CI, -2.15 to -0.94), whereas the interaction OR was 0.75 (95% CI, 0.52-1.10; P = 0.14). Baseline-to-later TPE use declined from 14% to 7% in principal-diagnosis AAV, 35% to 14% in AKI-D, and 32% to 23% with coded pulmonary hemorrhage. The length-of-stay-greater-than-1-day result was similar to the primary analysis. Inpatient TPE use among U.S. AAV hospitalizations declined during 2016-2023, including in multiple coded clinical-context sensitivities. The decline aligned with evolving trial evidence and guidelines, although these data cannot establish causation or appropriateness of treatment decisions.

items.title: Cutaneous and systemic manifestations of propylthiouracil-induced mpo-anca associated vasculitis: a case-based systematic review.
items.abstract: Propylthiouracil (PTU) is a well-established cause of drug-induced antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV), but cutaneous-limited presentations or isolated cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis (CSVV) require careful diagnostic evaluation. We report the case of a 37-year-old woman with Graves' disease treated with PTU for two years who presented with painful necrotic cutaneous ulcers involving the extremities, gluteal region, and earlobes (sparing auricular cartilage), accompanied by elevated MPO-ANCA titers and biopsy-proven leukocytoclastic vasculitis. Evaluation did not identify evidence of systemic vasculitis, infection, cryoglobulinemia, or an underlying malignancy. Prompt discontinuation of PTU resulted in progressive clinical remission within two months. A comprehensive systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases to identify all relevant published cases of PTU-induced MPO-ANCA-associated vasculitis with cutaneous manifestations. Eligibility screening and data extraction were performed following standard methodological criteria to synthesize clinical characteristics, management strategies, and patient outcomes.Synthesis of the literature confirmed a female predilection (93.3%), frequent MPO-ANCA/p-ANCA predominance, and variable exposure latencies ranging from 2 weeks to 11 years. Multi-organ involvement was common across the cohort, including renal manifestations, pulmonary complications, and musculoskeletal symptoms, alongside a subset presenting with strictly cutaneous-limited disease. Favorable outcomes were observed following PTU withdrawal and corticosteroids where indicated. PTU-induced MPO-ANCA-associated CSVV is an important diagnostic consideration. An accurate diagnosis relies on clinical, histopathological, and temporal data rather than ANCA positivity alone, and early drug cessation typically ensures a favorable prognosis.

items.title: Long-term progression of disease activity, organ damage, and symptom burden in Sjögren's disease: results from a prospective multicentre cohort.
items.abstract: To identify clinical and serological factors associated with progression of systemic activity, cumulative organ damage, and symptom burden in Sjögren's disease (SjD). We conducted a prospective multicenter study including 314 patients fulfilling the 2002 AECG classification criteria. After 9.5 years of follow up, progression was assessed across three domains: systemic activity (ESSDAI ≤4 to ≥5), organ damage (increase ≥1 point in SSDDI), and change in symptom burden (ESSPRI ≤4 to>4). Baseline variables were analyzed using bivariate tests and multivariable logistic regression. Among patients with low baseline systemic activity (ESSDAI ≤4), 55 of 213 (25.8%) had moderate-high activity (ESSDAI ≥5) at follow-up. In multivariable analysis, lymphadenopathy (OR 3.4, 95% CI 1.3-8.9), low C4 levels (OR 2.7, 95% CI 1.1-6.9), fibromyalgia (OR 5.4, 95% CI 2.3-12.4), and cataracts (OR 3.6, 95% CI 1.1-12.3) were independently associated with activity progression. Cumulative organ damage progressed in 63 patients (20.1%) and was independently associated with renal involvement (OR 3.2, 95% CI 1.2-8.2) and dyslipidemia (OR 2.2, 95% CI 1.1-4.5). In an exploratory analysis, 14 of 19 patients (73.7%) with baseline ESSPRI ≤4 had ESSPRI >4 at follow-up; no multivariable analysis was performed due to the small sample size. Systemic activity and cumulative damage increased in a substantial proportion of patients with SjD. Activity progression was independently associated with lymphadenopathy, C4 hypocomplementemia, fibromyalgia, and cataracts, while damage accrual was independently associated with renal involvement and dyslipidemia. These findings highlight the differential evolution of systemic activity, organ damage, and symptom burden, supporting their complementary assessment during long-term follow-up.

items.title: Social Determinants of Health and Disease Burden Among Medicare Advantage Enrollees With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus in the United States.
items.abstract: We evaluated social determinants of health (SDoH; conditions in which people are born, grow, live, work, and age) and health-related social needs (HRSNs; individual-level manifestations of SDoH) and their relationship with health outcomes in Medicare Advantage (MA) enrollees with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). This retrospective study included enrollees with SLE (18-89 years) and continuous enrollment during 2023. Disease severity and burden, treatment patterns, and SLE-related healthcare resource utilization were assessed using medical and pharmacy claims for SLE. Self-reported HRSNs were evaluated from a subgroup who completed a 2022 5-domain survey. Of 20,188 patients, 9,180 (45.5%) were <65 years and 11,008 (54.5%) ≥65 years. Most patients <65 years (98.3%, n=9,023) were eligible for Medicare through disability, versus 42.2% (n=4,646) ≥65 years. Patients <65 and ≥65 years with disability faced more adverse SDoH versus those ≥65 years without disability. Among HRSN survey respondents (n=615), 72.8% (n=448) reported ≥1 need and 20.3% (n=125) ≥3 needs; the proportion of patients classified as disabled, dual eligible, or eligible for low-income subsidy increased with greater HRSNs (HRSN=0, 44.3% [n=74]; HRSN≥3, 91.2% [n=114]). Respondents with ≥3 HRSNs had a greater burden of comorbid clinical conditions than those with no HRSNs. Our findings highlight the intersection between SDoH/HRSNs and disease burden among MA enrollees with SLE. Enrollment-based criteria (e.g., disability as original reason for entitlement and dual eligibility) were confirmed as practical signals for identifying those who may benefit from deeper assessments and targeted interventions, particularly in an aging population.

items.title: Subclinical shoulder tendinopathy in systemic lupus erythematosus: the SLE-SHEAR study.
items.abstract: BackgroundSubclinical tendon involvement in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) has been described mainly through fibrillar abnormalities and tenosynovitis, but structural and mechanical changes beyond synovial inflammation remain insufficiently characterised.ObjectiveTo compare ultrasound findings and shear-wave elastography measurements of supraspinatus and subscapularis tendons between asymptomatic SLE patients and matched healthy controls.MethodsForty-six asymptomatic female SLE patients and matched controls underwent standardised ultrasound and shear-wave elastography of the dominant shoulder. Elastography included predefined 5-mm 2 regions of interest in enthesic, middle and myotendinous sections of the supraspinatus tendon, and middle and myotendinous sections of the subscapularis tendon. Participants with abnormal physical examination findings underwent additional elastography of the contralateral shoulder, allowing within-subject comparisons between painful and non-painful shoulders.ResultsSLE patients showed higher frequencies of ultrasound-defined tendinosis and tenosynovitis than controls (e.g., supraspinatus tendinosis 36.9% vs 4.3%; subscapularis tendinosis 34.7% vs 2.1%). Tendon stiffness was lower in SLE patients, particularly in the supraspinatus middle (127.93 vs 150.82 kPa; p < 0.01) and subscapularis middle segments (100.72 vs 137.79 kPa; p < 0.001). Within the subgroup of SLE patients with abnormal physical examination findings, painful shoulders showed lower stiffness than contralateral non-painful shoulders, particularly in the supraspinatus mid-tendon and myotendinous regions.ConclusionAsymptomatic SLE patients exhibit imaging differences in tendon appearance and stiffness compared with matched controls. The biological mechanisms and clinical significance of these findings remain uncertain and require further investigation.

items.title: Gazing Upon the Great Eye: A Rare Presentation of Behcet's Disease.
items.abstract: Behcet's disease is a systemic autoimmune condition presenting classically with recurrent and painful mucocutaneous ulcers. It is more prevalent among Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, and Asian populations. Ocular or neurologic involvement is uncommon, but when present, contributes to significant morbidity and mortality (1). Clinical features are variable and often lead to delays in diagnosis (2). We report the case of a 41-year-old female who presented with left-sided pan-uveitis, shifting hypopyon, and retinitis. This followed several months of recurrent oral and genital ulcers, fevers, and constitutional symptoms. Her clinical course was complicated by subacute left lower limb sensory deficits and a new diagnosis of chronic hepatitis B virus infection. Anti-nuclear antibodies and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies were negative. She was HLA-B*51 positive. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed spinal lesions at the level of T6/T7 involving the right anterior and posterior horns, with possible involvement of the spinothalamic tract. The patient was initially treated with high-dose topical and systemic corticosteroids alongside entecavir, followed by regular infliximab infusions. Her uveitis and mucocutaneous symptoms significantly improved. A three-month progress MRI scan demonstrated radiological improvement with interval reduction in the size of the spinal lesions, though a degree of lower limb symptoms has persisted. This case illustrates the high morbidity associated with multi-organ manifestations of Behcet's disease. The heterogenous presentation may lead to diagnostic delays, and clinicians are reminded to consider less typical features of this potentially debilitating condition. A cross-disciplinary approach is particularly valuable and paramount to optimizing care for these patients.

items.title: Machine Learning Applied to Patient-Reported Outcomes and Passive Physiologic Sensor Data for Classification of Low Disease Activity in Rheumatoid Arthritis Patients.
items.abstract: We evaluated machine learning (ML) models using remotely collected patient-reported outcomes (ePROs) and wearable biosensor data to classify low disease activity (LDA) in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) following treatment initiation. RA patients with moderate-to-high disease activity (Clinical Disease Activity Index [CDAI]>10) initiating adalimumab or upadacitinib were enrolled from 28 U.S. rheumatology clinics and followed for approximately 3-6 months. AI models used baseline clinical variables and longitudinal daily and weekly ePROs, including PROMIS measures, RADAI-5, patient global assessment, and daily pain and fatigue numeric rating scale items; a subset contributed wearable data. ML models were trained to classify follow-up LDA (~12 weeks; CDAI≤10). Performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUCPR), and F1-based metrics, including positive predictive value-constrained F1. Among 150 participants with ePRO data, including 96 with wearable data, ePRO-based models achieved AUROCs of 0.745-0.857. Performance improved from 1- to 2-ePRO configurations, with limited gains from 2 to 3. The best weekly 2-ePRO generalized linear model rivaled more complex AI methods, with an AUROC of 0.843 and AUCPR 0.886. Reduced-Frequency data collection preserved predictive performance. Inclusion of wearable data did not improve performance in AI models and often resulted in lower discrimination, with wearable-only models demonstrating lower overall performance. Longitudinal ePRO-based ML models can classify follow-up LDA in RA using parsimonious, low-burden data collection strategies. Wearable data did not provide meaningful incremental value beyond ePROs, supporting the use of ePROs alone for routine remote monitoring of treatment response.

items.title: Adalimumab associated subacute thyroiditis in a patient with ankylosing spondylitis: A rare clinical entity.
items.abstract: BackgroundSubacute thyroiditis is a self-limiting granulomatous inflammatory disorder, most commonly precipitated by viral infection. Thyroiditis associated with adalimumab (Tumor necrosis factor alpha inhibitor) is rare, with limited case reports to date.Case ReportOur case describes a 40-year-old man with long-standing ankylosing spondylitis on adalimumab for 7 years, who presented with a month-long history of intermittent fever, neck pain and markedly elevated inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate). Biochemical thyrotoxicosis with diffusely reduced technetium-99m pertechnetate uptake on thyroid scan supported the diagnosis of subacute thyroiditis. An extensive evaluation excluded infectious and other autoimmune etiologies. Adalimumab therapy was suspected to be the likely precipitating factor. Prompt withdrawal of adalimumab and initiation of systemic corticosteroid therapy resulted in rapid clinical and biochemical resolution. The Naranjo adverse drug reaction probability score of 7 further supported a probable causal association.ConclusionThis case highlights the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for possibilities of biologic associated thyroiditis in patients receiving TNF-α inhibitors and presenting with fever of unknown origin.

items.title: Developing a patient-specific iPSC-derived monocyte model for familial Mediterranean fever and mevalonate kinase deficiency.
items.abstract: Autoinflammatory diseases (AIDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by dysregulation of the immune system. Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) and Mevalonate Kinase Deficiency (MKD) are two AIDs thought to converge on a shared pathway involving activation of the pyrin inflammasome. However, pathogenetic mechanisms leading to autoinflammation remain incompletely characterized. The rare nature of these diseases, along with genetic and interpersonal variations contribute to the difficulty of basic research. This study aims to establish a new patient-specific model system for the study of these rare diseases. 6 patients with clinical diagnoses of FMF or MKD-HIDS were included. Skin biopsies were used to establish primary fibroblast cultures. Patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cells were generated via transfection of episomal plasmids. Pluripotency was confirmed using qRT-PCR, immunofluorescence staining and in vitro trilineage differentiation. iPSC-derived monocytes were generated using STEMDiff Monocyte Kit and characterized with flow cytometry and immunofluorescence. In this study, we present patient-specific iPSCs for FMF and MKD-HIDS, providing the first MKD-HIDS specific iPSC model in the literature. We show these iPSCs are devoid of genomic aberrations, express pluripotency-related genes and can differentiate into three germ layers in vitro. We also used these iPSC lines for the generation iPSC-derived monocytes. We characterized the differentiated cells with flow cytometry and immunofluorescence. These patient-specific iPSCs enable a novel platform for functional research into FMF and MKD. Importantly, this study provides a proof-of-concept tool for functional studies investigating inflammasome activation and therapeutic responses in FMF and MKD in a patient-specific manner.

items.title: Mixed Reality-Based Telemedicine for Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis in a Remote Island Setting: Single-Center, Observational, Pilot Feasibility Study.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) requires regular specialist monitoring; however, access to rheumatologists is severely limited in remote island settings. Conventional 2D video-based telemedicine has limitations for detailed remote joint assessment. This study aimed to evaluate the technical and operational feasibility of the Nagasaki University Rheumatoid Arthritis Remote Medicine System (NURAS), a mixed reality (MR)-based telemedicine platform, for collaborative RA assessment in a remote island setting and to descriptively explore 12-month changes in clinical and patient-reported outcomes. NURAS enables remote rheumatologists to view 3D holographic joint images beyond conventional video telemedicine. In this 12-month single-center pilot feasibility study at Goto Chuoh Hospital, 6 patients with RA were enrolled. An on-site primary care physician and a remote rheumatologist at Nagasaki University Hospital jointly assessed patients at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months using a 28-joint count with real-time MR visualization. Primary outcomes were feasibility metrics, including the numbers of planned, attempted, completed, failed, and rescheduled sessions, connection interruptions, setup and consultation times, technical problems, and completion of planned joint assessments. Secondary outcomes were exploratory changes in disease activity (Disease Activity Score in 28 joints using C-reactive protein [DAS28-CRP] and Clinical Disease Activity Index [CDAI]) and patient-reported outcomes (Health Assessment Questionnaire Disability Index, Rheumatoid Arthritis Impact of Disease, Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Fatigue, pain visual analog scale, and Kessler 6-item psychological distress scale), summarized as medians with IQRs. This study was a noninterventional observational feasibility study and was not prospectively registered. The study was approved by the Nagasaki University Hospital Clinical Research Ethics Committee (approval 21081605). All 18 planned telemedicine sessions were attempted and completed; 2 sessions were rescheduled for patient-related reasons, and no connection interruptions were documented. All planned joint assessments were completed, and setup required approximately 5 minutes per session with assistance from 1 nurse. Median consultation time was 37 minutes 45 seconds (IQR 33 minutes 19 seconds-47 minutes 34 seconds) at baseline and 17 minutes 47 seconds (IQR 15 minutes 16 seconds-20 minutes 38 seconds) at 12 months. Median DAS28-CRP decreased from 2.98 (IQR 2.60-3.61) to 1.69 (IQR 1.19-1.79) and median CDAI from 10.0 (IQR 7.1-13.0) to 3.0 (IQR 1.0-5.0), whereas patient-reported outcomes varied across individuals. Clinical outcome changes were interpreted descriptively. NURAS was technically and operationally feasible for collaborative, specialist-supported RA care in a remote island setting. Larger controlled studies are needed to evaluate diagnostic agreement, acceptability, technical performance, cost, and clinical effectiveness.

items.title: Associations Between Lipid Parameters and Disease Activity in Anti-CCP-Positive and Anti-CCP-Negative Rheumatoid Arthritis Patients.
items.abstract: To investigate the associations between lipid parameters and disease activity in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) stratified by anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibody status, and to evaluate their discriminative performance for moderate-to-high disease activity. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 292 patients with RA (224 anti-CCP-positive and 68 anti-CCP-negative) and 319 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Alongside clinical and laboratory profiling, disease activity was quantified using the 28-joint Disease Activity Score based on C-reactive protein (DAS28-CRP). Associations of individual lipid parameters with DAS28-CRP were evaluated via Spearman correlation and separate multivariable linear regression models adjusting for age, sex, and disease duration, and additionally for medications, comorbidities, and body mass index (BMI) in sensitivity analyses. Discrimination for moderate-to-high disease activity was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Compared with healthy controls, patients with RA demonstrated significantly lower total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1), and apolipoprotein B (ApoB) levels, alongside higher lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)], whereas lipid profiles were comparable across anti-CCP subgroups. In the anti-CCP-positive subgroup, TC, HDL-C, LDL-C, and ApoA1 correlated inversely with DAS28-CRP, while Lp(a) and the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio correlated positively; following multivariable adjustment, all associations except Lp(a) persisted. In the anti-CCP-negative subgroup, only the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio retained an independent association with DAS28-CRP, without significant effect modification by anti-CCP status. These inverse associations remained largely robust in sensitivity analyses. Lipid markers provided modest discriminative value for moderate-to-high disease activity, yielding area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.635 for TC and 0.627 for combined ApoA1 and Lp(a). Specific lipid parameters are independently associated with disease activity in RA, most notably within the anti-CCP-positive subgroup. Despite modest standalone discriminative performance for moderate-to-high disease activity, routine lipid profiling may serve as an accessible, complementary indicator of systemic inflammatory burden, meriting prospective longitudinal validation.

items.title: Atypical Neurological Presentation of Familial Mediterranean Fever Mimicking Refractory Childhood Epilepsy.
items.abstract: Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) is a monogenic autoinflammatory disorder classically characterized by recurrent episodes of fever and polyserositis. Although central nervous system involvement is rare, FMF can atypically present with severe neurological manifestations, including seizure disorders. The authors report the highly unusual case of a 27-year-old male who was misdiagnosed with West syndrome at 8 months of age and was subsequently treated with multiple antiepileptic drugs (AEDs) for over 2 decades. The patient was initially referred for the evaluation of chronically elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) and serum amyloid A (SAA) levels of unknown etiology. A detailed medical history revealed recurrent episodes of paradoxical abdominal pain. Genetic analysis identified heterozygous R202Q and M680I mutations in the MEFV gene, establishing the diagnosis of FMF. Strikingly, the initiation of targeted autoinflammatory therapy with colchicine not only normalized his systemic inflammatory markers but also resulted in complete seizure freedom. This profound clinical response enabled the successful withdrawal of his long-term AED polytherapy. This case highlights that refractory, childhood-onset epilepsy can occasionally serve as an atypical neurological mask for FMF. Clinicians must consider autoinflammatory etiologies in patients with treatment-resistant seizures and unexplained systemic inflammation, as targeted therapy can safely reverse years of unnecessary antiepileptic treatment. Cite this article as: Berkkan M, Er Gülbezer, E. Atypical neurological presentation of familial Mediterranean fever mimicking refractory childhood epilepsy. Eur J Rheumatol. 2026, 13(2), 0027, doi:10.5152/eurjrheum.2026.26027.

items.title: The Companionship of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Qualitative Study of Embodiment and Time With a Chronic Autoimmune Disease.
items.abstract: Women with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) live with an unpredictable, chronic autoimmune disease that profoundly alters embodied existence over time. While clinical research has focused on symptom management and self-care, the existential dimensions of living permanently with SLE remain understudied. Using van Manen's hermeneutic phenomenology and a longitudinal qualitative design extending across a year and a half with three interview rounds, this study, part of a larger research project, explored how 15 women with SLE developed an embodied, existential relationship with their disease across time. One essential phenomenon was interpreted as constitutive of the women's lived experience: being in a companionship with SLE. This companionship, uninvited, embodied, and permanent, unfolded through three interrelated aspects: concealing SLE, living in embodied alertness, and living in a fragile balance. Together, these trace an existential arc from early resistance and concealment toward a strained but manageable coexistence with the illness as a permanent condition of life. The findings carry implications for nursing practice, providing a basis for developing existentially attuned, phenomenologically informed patient education and rehabilitation in rheumatology. Kvinder med systemisk lupus erythematosus (SLE) lever med en uforudsigelig, kronisk autoimmun sygdom, der over tid grundlæggende forandrer den kropslige tilværelse. Mens sygeplejeforskningen primært har fokuseret på symptomhåndtering og egenomsorg, er de eksistentielle dimensioner ved at leve med SLE, som et livsvilkår, fortsat utilstrækkeligt belyst. Med udgangspunkt i van Manens hermeneutiske fænomenologi og et longitudinelt kvalitativt design, blev 15 kvinder med SLE fulgt over en periode på 1,5 år med tre interviewrunder. Studiet her, der er sidste del af et større forskningsprojekt, undersøgte, hvordan et kropsligt og eksistentielt forhold til sygdom udfoldede sig over tid. Ét væsentligt fænomen blev fortolket som konstitutivt for kvindernes levede erfaring over tid: at være i et livsledsagerskab med SLE. Dette livsledsagerskab, ufrivilligt, kropsligt og permanent, udfoldede sig gennem tre indbyrdes forbundne aspekter: at skjule SLE, at leve i kropslig årvågenhed og at leve i en skrøbelig balance. Tilsammen tegner disse en eksistentiel retning fra tidlig modstand og fortielse hen imod et belastet, men håndterbart samliv med sygdommen som en permanent livsbetingelse. Studiets fund har implikationer for sygeplejepraksis og kan medvirke til udvikling af eksistentielt afstemt patientuddannelse og rehabilitering i reumatologien.

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of Filgotinib in Psoriatic Arthritis: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Psoriatic arthritis (PsA) is a chronic inflammatory disease affecting musculoskeletal and cutaneous domains. Filgotinib, a preferential Janus kinase 1 inhibitor, has been investigated as a targeted oral therapy for PsA. To evaluate the short-term efficacy and safety of filgotinib vs placebo in adults with PsA and assess the certainty of the evidence using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). The study was designed as a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to October 2025. Three RCTs involving 295 participants (173 receiving filgotinib and 122 receiving placebo) were included. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated risk ratios (RRs) for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences (MDs) for continuous outcomes. Efficacy was assessed at weeks 12 and 16, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. At week 16, filgotinib increased American College of Rheumatology 20% response (RR, 1.91, 95% CI, 1.38 to 2.64), minimal disease activity achievement (RR, 1.73, 95% CI, 1.05 to 2.85), and Psoriatic Arthritis Response Criteria response (RR, 1.59, 95% CI, 1.27 to 1.98). Psoriasis Area and Severity Index 75% response was also higher (RR, 2.68, 95% CI, 1.78 to 4.02). Psoriatic Arthritis Disease Activity Score improved (MD, -1.03, 95% CI, -1.42 to -0.63; 277 participants). No statistically significant differences were detected in serious adverse events (RR, 1.58, 95% CI, 0.29 to 8.69) or all-cause mortality (RR, 3.05, 95% CI, 0.13 to 73.42); these estimates were imprecise. Filgotinib demonstrated short-term efficacy across several PsA outcomes. However, 3 short-term RCTs with limited safety events cannot establish long-term safety or comparative effectiveness. Filgotinib is not approved for PsA, and its clinical role remains unestablished. PROSPERO CRD420251235155.

items.title: Sustained target attainment in psoriatic arthritis: Predictors and barriers in a Chinese longitudinal cohort.
items.abstract: The multidimensional clinical manifestations of PsA encompassing challenges to both the definition and consistent implementation of T2T in this population. A key hurdle is the lack of consensus regarding the optimal approach to disease activity assessment. Yet studies reveal considerable disparities in target attainment rates depending on the instrument used. To date, no longitudinal cohort data have been available on the attainment and sustainability of treatment targets among Chinese patients with PsA. Treat-to-target improves outcomes in psoriatic arthritis (PsA), but the optimal target definition and sustainability of disease control remain unclear. We therefore systematically compared five composite measures for assessing treatment target attainment and identified predictors of sustained disease control in a Chinese PsA cohort. This cross-sectional and retrospective cohort study, based on the PKUPsA cohort (2016-2024), compared five PsA response criteria (MDA, DAPSA, cDAPSA, DAS28-ESR, DAS28-CRP) at baseline and evaluated short-term and sustained attainment/remission over 12 months of follow-up, exploring predictors of sustained response. Data from the Peking University First Hospital PsA (PKUPsA) cohort (enrolled 2016-2024) were analyzed. Baseline rates of target attainment were compared across five definitions: DAPSA, cDAPSA, DAS28-ESR, DAS28-CRP, and MDA. A longitudinal subcohort was followed for sustained treatment target attainment. Agreement between measures was evaluated with Cohen's Kappa, and predictors of sustained attainment were identified via Cox regression. Among 419 patients (59.2% male, median age 49 years, disease duration 2 years), baseline target attainment varied significantly: 33.4% (MDA), 54.4% (DAPSA), 58.5% (DAS28-ESR), 62.1% (DAS28-CRP), and 62.5% (cDAPSA). Measure Agreement ranged from moderate to excellent (Kappa: 0.417-0.834). In DAPSA-but not MDA-attainers, pain VAS (82.1%) and PASI (77.9%) were the main limiting factors. In the longitudinal cohort (n=151), 6-month sustained treatment target attainment ranged from 35.1% (MDA) to 71.3% (cDAPSA), with marked declines over longer periods. Factors associated with faster sustained attainment included lower baseline disease activity (VAS ≤3, TJC68 ≤3, SJC66 ≤3, HAQ ≤1, CRP ≤5 mg/L, ESR ≤13 mm/h). For sustained remission, predictors included lower baseline TJC68, VAS, HAQ, CRP, and baseline csDMARD use. In this first systematic evaluation of five composite measures for sustained targets in a Chinese PsA cohort, short-term success was achievable but long-term sustainability remained challenging. Lower baseline disease activity was associated with faster achievement of sustained targets, whereas baseline csDMARD use was associated with sustained remission; these observational associations should not be interpreted as evidence of therapeutic superiority. These findings support standardized, clinically feasible assessment strategies to improve PsA management. Psoriatic arthritis (PsA) is a long-term disease that causes joint pain, stiffness, and swelling in people with psoriasis. Doctors increasingly use a treat-to-target approach, agreeing on a clear goal at the start of treatment, then adjusting therapy until the patient reaches it. However, experts disagree on which measurement tool best shows whether a patient is doing well. We studied 419 patients with PsA treated at Peking University First Hospital between 2016 and 2024. We compared five commonly used scoring systems at the start of treatment, then followed 151 of these patients for 12 months to see who stayed at their goal over time. The five tools often gave different answers. At the start, only one-third of patients met the strictest goal (MDA), while nearly two-thirds met the loosest one (cDAPSA). After six months, between 35% and 71% of patients reached their goal, depending on the tool, and fewer stayed at goal afterwards. Patients who began treatment with milder symptoms (less pain, fewer swollen joints, lower inflammation, and better daily functioning) were more likely to reach and keep their target. Those already on conventional disease-modifying drugs were more likely to remain in remission. In contrast, patients with higher pain or more swollen joints at the start had a harder time staying at goal. In short, short-term success is achievable, but keeping the disease under control over many months is difficult. Choosing one agreed-upon, practical way to measure progress could help doctors treat PsA more consistently and improve long-term outcomes for patients.

items.title: Genetic and multi-omic insights into inflammation and metabolism in a French Polynesian cohort.
items.abstract: Inflammatory and metabolic diseases are a major global health burden, and their genetic mechanisms differ between populations. The stepwise settlement of the Pacific has left Polynesian communities with variants that are locally common and globally rare. Yet these communities remain underrepresented in genomic research. Here we combine whole-genome sequencing with blood metabolite and gene-activity profiling in a gout-focused cohort of 1,043 French Polynesian participants, and show that such variants shape molecular traits and disease risk. Hundreds alter metabolite levels, gene expression or splicing but are absent or rare in global reference datasets. Findings include a gene-disrupting variant in ANGPTL8 that lowers lipids and inflammatory markers; an LRMDA variant linked to type 2 diabetes; and a signal at the alpha-globin locus suggestive of thalassemia trait. Integrating molecular and phenotypic data further implicates WDR1 as an additional causal gout gene at the SLC2A9 locus. Genomic research in underrepresented populations thus reveals broadly relevant disease mechanisms.

items.title: An Unusual Association of Adult-Onset Still's Disease, Aseptic Meningitis, and Concurrent Celiac Disease in a Young Patient.
items.abstract: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a rare systemic autoinflammatory disorder that presents a diagnostic challenge for many clinicians because of its heterogeneous clinical manifestations and overlap with infectious and other inflammatory conditions. In contrast, celiac disease is a common immune-mediated disorder triggered by gluten ingestion, which damages the small intestine and prevents proper nutrient absorption. It affects only a small proportion of the global population. We present the case of a 24-year-old woman who was initially hospitalized with abdominal pain, high-grade fever, and sore throat, accompanied by leukocytosis and abnormal liver function tests, and later developed altered mental status. An extensive rheumatologic evaluation was negative; however, serologic testing for celiac disease was positive, and the diagnosis was subsequently confirmed by esophagogastroduodenoscopy with duodenal biopsy. The patient also met the Yamaguchi criteria for AOSD with concomitant aseptic meningitis presentation. AOSD-associated aseptic meningitis is uncommon, and its coexistence with newly diagnosed celiac disease has not been reported in the literature. This case highlights the importance of considering AOSD in patients presenting with aseptic meningitis and systemic inflammatory features, particularly when an infectious etiology is not identified. Early recognition and prompt initiation of appropriate therapy are essential for better clinical outcomes.

items.title: Intramuscular Vitamin D2 in Patients With Systemic Sclerosis Not Responding to Oral Supplementation: A Retrospective Observational Case Series.
items.abstract: Background This study aimed to evaluate changes in serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) levels following intramuscular (IM) ergocalciferol in patients with systemic sclerosis (SSc) and persistently low levels (<30 ng/mL) despite at least six months of oral cholecalciferol supplementation. Clinical outcomes of SSc were not assessed. Methodology This retrospective series included patients with SSc who received IM vitamin D2 after non-response to oral supplementation. Non-response was defined as a serum 25(OH)D level remaining below 30 ng/mL after at least six months of oral cholecalciferol at a dose of 10,000 IU weekly. Serum 25(OH)D was measured before the first injection, two weeks after the first injection, and four weeks after the second injection. Results In total, 12 patients were identified, with a mean age of 47.8 years; all were women. Five patients had diffuse cutaneous SSc, while seven had limited cutaneous SSc. The mean disease duration was 17.9 years, with a mean modified Rodnan skin score of 14.9. All patients received two injections of 300,000 IU of ergocalciferol into the anterior gluteus muscle at a 15-day interval. The mean serum 25(OH)D level rose from 12.9 ng/mL before the first injection to 23.1 ng/mL two weeks after the first injection, and to 37.2 ng/mL four weeks after the second injection (p < 0.001). Overall, 10 of the 12 patients reached a level of 30 ng/mL or higher. No adverse events were reported during the follow-up period. Conclusions In this small retrospective series, IM ergocalciferol increased serum 25(OH)D levels and was not associated with reported adverse events. Prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings.

items.title: Serum β-γ bridging on capillary zone electrophoresis as a clue for suspecting immunoglobulin G4-related disease: a case report.
items.abstract: Diagnosis of immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4)-related disease is challenging due to heterogeneous clinical presentations and histologic overlap with lymphoproliferative disorders. We report a case of a 62-year-old man who presented with a pulmonary lesion on imaging and lymphadenopathy, initially suspicious for lymphoma. Biopsy revealed T-cell lymphoma-like features, with prominent plasma cell infiltration. Serum immunoglobulin levels and capillary zone electrophoresis were performed, followed by targeted serum IgG4 measurement and immunohistochemical staining. Serum IgG levels were markedly elevated at 31.32 g/L (reference range, 7.6-16.6 g/L), whereas IgA (1.55 g/L [reference range, 0.71-3.35 g/L]) and IgM (0.86 g/L [reference range, 0.48-2.12 g/L]) were both within normal limits. Capillary zone electrophoresis demonstrated a distinct β-γ bridging pattern, prompting targeted IgG4 quantification, which was strikingly elevated at 24.8 g/L (reference range, 0.03-2.01 g/L-more than 12 times the upper limit of normal) and accounted for approximately 79% of total serum IgG. Immunohistochemistry confirmed dense IgG4-positive plasma cell infiltration accompanied by storiform fibrosis, supporting IgG4-related disease as a leading differential diagnosis. This case underscores that β-γ bridging on serum electrophoresis can serve as an accessible and valuable clue to IgG4-related disease in ambiguous presentations, guiding targeted serologic and pathologic verification, thereby facilitating timely diagnostic workup and appropriate disease management.

items.title: Traditional Chinese medicine collaborative care in the management of patients with axial spondyloarthritis: long-term outcomes of a pragmatic randomised controlled trial through week 52.
items.abstract: Acupuncture has been postulated to have analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects. We report the secondary outcomes through week 52 of a pragmatic randomised controlled trial that evaluated the effectiveness of a Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) collaborative model of care (TCMCMC) involving acupuncture in patients with axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). Primary and exploratory outcomes reported previously showed that the intervention group had improved spinal pain, disease activity and disease-specific quality of life at week 6. Eligible patients with active axSpA were randomised to intervention or control group. The intervention group received TCMCMC (10 TCM consultations and acupuncture over the first five weeks). Both intervention and control groups received usual rheumatologic care. Secondary outcomes through 52 weeks over follow-up time-points at weeks 6, 12, 24 and 52 included spinal pain, Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI), Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index (BASFI), Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Patient Global Score (BAS-G), Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ), 36-item Short Form survey (SF-36) and Ankylosing Spondylitis Quality of Life (ASQoL). Repeated measures analyses were conducted using linear mixed models. A total of 139 patients were recruited, with 70 and 69 assigned to the intervention and control group respectively. Using a linear mixed model, the average treatment effects across weeks 6, 12, 24 and 52 for spinal pain, BASDAI, BASFI, HAQ, BAS-G, SF-36 Physical Component Summary, SF-36 Mental Component Summary and ASQoL were not statistically significant. The TCMCMC approach showed short-term benefits in spinal pain, disease activity and disease-specific quality of life at week 6 compared to usual rheumatologic care, but benefits were not sustained through 52 weeks. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03420404 (registered on 14 February 2018).

items.title: Integrative multi-omic mapping of urinary and intrarenal immune landscapes in lupus nephritis identifies convergent inflammatory and fibrotic programs.
items.abstract: Renal biopsy is the gold standard for classifying lupus nephritis (LN), but due to its invasiveness and difficult longitudinal follow-up, it incompletely captures immune and histopathological dynamics. Urinary single-cell transcriptomic analysis has been proposed as a minimally invasive approach for monitoring LN, while renal single-cell and spatial transcriptomics provide high-resolution reference maps of the intrarenal environment. We performed a systematic scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines to evaluate direct urinary-renal transcriptomic concordance and pathway molecular convergence of single-cell, single-nucleus, spatial transcriptomic studies. PubMed/MEDLINE and GEO Datasets were systematically searched on August 27, 2026, to identify this concordance and convergence in LN. Analysis of 53 studies identified just one direct urinary-renal transcriptomic concordance study but broader pathway-level biological convergence evidence. Transcriptomic concordance (Tier I) identified shared interferon-responsive signatures, particularly IFIT1, IFIT3, IFI44, MX1 , and OAS1; but pathway convergence studies (supported by Tier II studies) gave insights into major urinary biomarkers, such as CXCL9/CXCL10, IL-16, sCD163, BAFF, and FABP4, linked to renal transcriptomic or histopathological programs. The strongest urinary-renal convergence involved IFN signaling and chemokine-mediated immune trafficking, followed by macrophage-associated inflammation and fibrotic remodeling. Collectively, these signatures and biomarkers support urinary profiling as a complementary minimally invasive strategy for longitudinal monitoring and precision nephrology.

items.title: Immunometabolic mechanisms across psoriatic disease: linking psoriasis to psoriatic arthritis.
items.abstract: Psoriatic disease encompasses cutaneous and musculoskeletal inflammation. The mechanisms determining why some patients with psoriasis develop psoriatic arthritis while others do not remain incompletely understood. Current models emphasise the IL-23/IL-17 axis and tumour necrosis factor signalling, but cytokine-centric explanations do not fully account for tissue tropism, heterogeneous clinical trajectories, or preclinical musculoskeletal involvement. In this review, we examine immunometabolism as an additional regulatory layer linking systemic immune activation, tissue-specific susceptibility, and local inflammatory amplification across the psoriatic disease spectrum. We summarise evidence implicating glycolysis, mitochondrial dysfunction, amino acid metabolism, lipid metabolism, bile acid pathways, adipokines, and collagen-related metabolites in cutaneous, circulating, synovial, and entheseal compartments. We propose a multi-compartment model in which systemic immunometabolic priming interacts with pre-lesional skin dysregulation and receptive musculoskeletal niches to shape whether inflammation manifests in the skin, joints, entheses, or a combination. This model reframes psoriatic arthritis not simply as a downstream extension of cutaneous inflammation but as one manifestation of a broader systemic disorder in which metabolic and immune pathways converge. Finally, we consider clinical implications for risk prediction, diagnostic refinement, therapeutic stratification, and metabolic intervention, highlighting the need for longitudinal, multi-omics studies that integrate serum, skin, synovial, entheseal, imaging, and clinical data to identify patients at risk before irreversible musculoskeletal damage occurs.

items.title: Evaluation of optical coherence tomography angiography findings in patients with Behçet's disease and comparison with healthy eyes.
items.abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate retinal, choroidal, and optic nerve head microvascular alterations in patients with Behçet's disease using optical coherence tomography angiography. This prospective cross-sectional study included 116 eyes of 58 patients with Behçet's disease and 60 eyes of 30 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Patients with Behçet's disease were divided into two groups: those with a history of ocular involvement who were clinically inactive at the time of examination and those without a history of ocular involvement. Optical coherence tomography angiography was used to measure superficial capillary plexus and deep capillary plexus vascular density (%) and flow area (mm 2 ). Choriocapillaris, optic nerve head, and radial peripapillary capillary flow areas, as well as foveal avascular zone area, were also analyzed. In both Behçet's disease groups, Superficial capillary plexus and deep capillary plexus flow areas vascular density and flow area values were significantly lower than those of the healthy control group (p < 0.001, for all comparisons). In the clinically inactive ocular Behçet disease group, Superficial capillary plexus vascular density was found to be lower than in the group without ocular involvement (p = 0.011). Optic nerve head and flow area was significantly reduced in the clinically inactive ocular Behçet group compared with both the non-ocular Behçet group (p = 0.006) and the control group (p < 0.001). Radial peripapillary capillary flow area values were significantly lower in both Behçet disease groups compared with the control group (p < 0.001; p = 0.006, respectively). Optical coherence tomography angiography appears to be an effective adjunctive imaging modality for evaluating retinal, choroidal, and optic disc microvascular structures in Behçet's disease regardless of ocular involvement and across all stages of the disease.

items.title: Ocular Screening in Children With Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis or Treated With Hydroxychloroquine: Clinical Report.
items.abstract: Ophthalmic screening examinations are critical in children at risk for inflammatory ocular diseases or toxicity from medication use. Children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) who are at risk for or have had a diagnosis of uveitis require scheduled ophthalmic examinations. Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) is a treatment for several pediatric diseases and has a risk for retinal toxicity. Guidance is needed on the frequency of ophthalmic screening and the critical tests to be performed in both settings. Clinicians are highly encouraged to follow adult HCQ dosing recommendations (<5 mg/kg actual weight) until there are more specific data for children. This clinical report addresses recommendations for ophthalmic examinations in children with JIA, children with JIA-associated uveitis, and children receiving HCQ treatment. Families should be counseled about the critical importance of regular screening examinations for reducing the risk of visual impairment from disease-associated complications or medication toxicity. They can be reassured about the relative safety of medical therapy for these conditions if screening guidelines are followed.

items.title: Platelet-neutrophil immunothrombosis in obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome and non-APS pregnancy morbidity during low-molecular-weight heparin-based prophylaxis.
items.abstract: We prospectively studied 21 women receiving low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) for APS or non-APS pregnancy morbidity and 21 healthy pregnant controls. Ten women were reassessed two years after LMWH discontinuation. Reference groups comprised 21 age-matched healthy non-pregnant women and five non-pregnant patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Blood was collected at 10-12, 20-22 and 30-34 weeks of gestation. Platelet and neutrophil activation, platelet-neutrophil aggregates and myeloperoxidase (MPO)-DNA complexes were quantified. Longitudinal biomarkers were analysed using participant-level mixed-effects models including study group, gestational stage and their interaction. LMWH effects were examined in vitro, and ex vivo NET generation was assessed in neutrophils from treated high-risk and untreated healthy pregnancies. Healthy pregnancy was associated with increased platelet P-selectin expression and MPO-DNA complexes, without broad neutrophil activation. Women reassessed off LMWH showed substantially higher platelet HMGB1, platelet-neutrophil aggregates, neutrophil tissue factor expression and MPO-DNA complexes than non-pregnant controls, with exploratory within-participant analyses supporting increases from pregnancy to postpartum. During LMWH treatment, most markers fell within the distributions observed in healthy pregnancy. Mixed-effects models provided no multiplicity-adjusted evidence of differences in gestational trajectories between healthy and treated pregnancies. In vitro, LMWH attenuated platelet activation and platelet-driven neutrophil responses, while neutrophils from LMWH-treated patients showed reduced ex vivo responsiveness. All index pregnancies resulted in live births. These findings indicate that platelet activation characterises healthy pregnancy. During LMWH treatment, most markers of platelet-neutrophil activation show distributions close to those observed in healthy pregnancy.Top of Form.

items.title: Sex differences in ischemic heart disease mortality among patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a literature review.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular Diseases (CVD) are the leading cause of mortality among patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA), exhibiting incidence rates significantly higher than those in the Reference Population (RP). Chronic inflammation, traditional cardiovascular risk factors, and potential adverse effects of RA treatments contribute to this increased risk. This literature review examined sex differences in Ischemic Heart Disease (IHD) mortality among RA patients. We searched PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library using the keywords "rheumatoid arthritis AND cardiovascular disease OR ischemic heart disease AND mortality". We included observational studies, reviews, and meta-analyses published in English until April 2022. Eligible studies reported data separately for males and females. Outcomes were analyzed for differences in IHD mortality relative to the RP and between sexes. Of 43 primary studies on CVD, 6 examined IHD mortality in men and women separately. Study durations ranged from 4- to 21-years, with follow-up periods averaging 7.05- to 11.4-years. Female participants represented 53.2% to 74.0% of the sample, with a mean age of 54.0- to 60.4-years. The total sample size included 47,144 patients. In four out of five studies, the Standardized Mortality Ratio (SMR) for IHD was higher in women with RA compared to the RP (SMR range: 1.41-1.95). Among men, three of five studies reported an SMR higher than the RP (range: 1.41-1.63). One study found that the risk of IHD mortality was greater in women than in men. Another study, using the age-adjusted incidence rate ratio, found higher IHD mortality in RA patients compared to the non-arthritis group (women: 1.6; men: 1.4) but noted no conclusive sex differences. IHD mortality in RA patients was higher than in RP, both for women and men. Women lost their typical protective advantage of a later onset of IHD, highlighting RA's substantial impact on cardiovascular outcomes in women.

items.title: Integrating UHPLC-Q/TOF MS, network pharmacology and experimental validation to reveal the potential mechanisms and bioactive components of Zhuang medicine Longzuan Tongbi granules against rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Longzuan Tongbi granules (LZTBG), a clinically validated eight-herb Zhuang medicine formula containing alkaloids, flavonoids, coumarins, and lignans, exerts anti-RA effects through multi-component, multi-target regulation. However, due to the complexity of its chemical composition, the anti-RA material basis and underlying mechanisms of LZTBG have not been systematically explored. The objective of this study was to identify the active components and molecular mechanisms of LZTBG in the therapy of RA. The chemical constituents of LZTBG were comprehensively characterized using UHPLC-Q/TOF MS coupled with feature-based molecular networking (FBMN). Serum pharmacochemistry was performed to identify absorbed components and investigate their in vivo metabolic patterns in rats. Network pharmacology combined with previously published metabolomics data was employed to predict core targets and potential regulatory pathways. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were conducted to validate target-ligand interactions. Finally, in vitro experiments using LPS-induced RAW264.7 macrophages were performed to verify the anti-RA effects and underlying mechanisms of the candidate compounds via ELISA, qRT-PCR, and Western blot analyses. A total of 235 chemical constituents were characterized in LZTBG, with alkaloids and coumarins identified as major active types. Serum pharmacochemistry detected 74 LZTBG-related compounds in rat plasma, revealing structure-dependent disparities in metabolic behaviors. Network pharmacology integrated with metabolomics highlighted ALOX5, MAPK3, and PIK3CA as core targets, with ALOX5 prioritized based on high-confidence protein-protein interaction evidence and topological significance. KEGG enrichment indicated primary involvement of lipid and atherosclerosis pathways. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated that bergapten, magnoflorine, and marmesin bound stably to these targets, with MAPK and ALOX5 complexes displaying optimal structural stability. In vitro validation confirmed that these compounds significantly suppressed LPS-induced upregulation of IL-1β and TNF-α, downregulated ALOX5, MAPK3, and PIK3CA mRNA and protein expression, and inhibited ERK1/2 phosphorylation in a dose-dependent manner. This study systematically elucidates that bergapten, magnoflorine, and marmesin are the principal active components of LZTBG against RA. The therapeutic effects are mediated through multi-component, multi-target regulation of the MAPK/ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling pathways and their downstream inflammatory target ALOX5. The integration of multi-omics data with experimental validation provides a robust paradigm for deciphering the complex mechanisms of traditional medicines and highlights ALOX5 as a promising therapeutic target for RA intervention.

items.title: Efficacy, adverse drug reactions, and symptom relief from different doses of tofacitinib combined with methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy of tofacitinib (TOF) at different doses combined with methotrexate (MTX) in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and their effects on adverse drug reactions (ADRs) and symptom relief. The study enrolled 123 patients with RA treated at the Second Hospital of Lanzhou University (February 2023 to February 2026), divided by TOF dose into a low-dose group (5 mg/day, n=60) and a high-dose group (10 mg/day, n=63). Outcomes compared between the two groups included treatment efficacy; adverse drug reactions (ADRs) (transient hepatic dysfunction, leukopenia, upper respiratory infection, nausea/vomiting, rash, and diarrhea); symptom relief (tender joint count (TJC), swollen joint count (SJC), and morning stiffness duration); pain (Visual Analogue Scale (VAS)); disease activity (Disease Activity Score 28 (DAS28)); inflammatory markers (interleukin (IL)-6, IL-17, and interferon (IFN)-γ); bone turnover markers (osteocalcin (BGP) and procollagen type 1 N-terminal propeptide (PINP)); other laboratory indices (erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), rheumatoid factor (RF), and C-reactive protein (CRP)); and quality of life (36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36)). Finally, this study stratified patients by baseline DAS28 and inflammatory and bone turnover markers for subgroup analysis. The high-dose group showed superior efficacy to the low-dose group (P=0.045) and a comparable ADR rate (P>0.05), with lower post-treatment TJC, SJC, morning stiffness duration, VAS, DAS28, IL-6, IL-17, IFN-γ, ESR, RF, and CRP (all P<0.05) and higher post-treatment BGP, PINP, and SF-36 scores (all P<0.05). In addition, no significant interaction was observed between the treatment groups and baseline DAS28, inflammatory markers, or bone turnover markers. High-dose TOF + MTX was highly effective in treating RA, providing effective symptom relief without significantly increasing ADRs; moreover, the effect may not be significantly affected by baseline disease activity, inflammation level, or bone turnover status.

items.title: Oral health, oral follow-up and infectious risk management of rheumatoid arthritis patients on anti-TNF drugs: a survey of a French e-cohort.
items.abstract: As periodontitis is a recognized risk factor for rheumatoid arthritis (RA), it should be adequately treated before the initiation of biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs), along with any concomitant acute oral infection. bDMARDs remains a concern for patients, and can pose challenges for dentists, particularly regarding the management of invasive procedures. Our aim was to assess adherence to oral health recommendations, and perioperative management of invasive dental procedures in RA patients with bDMARDs. A French online cross-sectional survey was conducted within the ART e-cohort. A semi-structured 77-item questionnaire was developed by a multidisciplinary team (rheumatologists, dentists, expert patients). Validated oral health scores (Oral Health Impact Profile [OHIP-14] and Periodontal Screening Score [PESS]) were calculated from responses and combined with routine cohort data (RAPID-3, EQ-5D-5 L). Of 543 e-cohort participants, 279 completed the survey (response rate 51.4%; 71% female; 70% aged ≥ 50 years). RA duration exceeded 5 years in 63.7%. Most participants (90%) were receiving bDMARD, including 67% on anti-TNF. Moderate-to-severe RA activity was common (53% with RAPID-3 ≥ 7). The mean EQ-5D-5 L index was 0.605. Based on a PESS > 5 41.6% of respondents were identified at risk of severe periodontitis. The risk increased with age, smoking, alcohol consumption, and RA severity, but was not associated with treatment type. Only 16.5% of participants fully adhered to French professional oral health recommendations, including twice-daily tooth brushing, interdental cleaning and annual dental check-ups). One in four patients had undergone invasive dental procedures within 2 years; 68.5% continued bDMARD therapy. Post-operative complications were rare, all after extractions without antibiotic cover. In the present cohort, RA patients showed low adherence to oral health recommendations and high risk of severe periodontitis. Postoperative complications while continuing bDMARDs were infrequent.

items.title: Socioeconomic inequalities in psoriatic arthritis treatment in Brazil: a nationwide analysis of coverage, use and expenditure.
items.abstract: Psoriatic arthritis (PsA) is a chronic inflammatory immune-mediated disease associated with significant impairment and reduced quality of life. Despite the availability of a clinical protocol within the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS), the coverage and socioeconomic distribution of pharmacological treatment for PsA across federative units remain uncharacterized. This study analysed territorial and socioeconomic inequalities in PsA treatment coverage, use, and expenditure in Brazil in 2025. A nationwide cross-sectional study was conducted using administrative data from the SUS Outpatient Information System (SIA/SUS - APAC). The eligible population (PAT_ SUS ) was estimated from GBD 2023 psoriasis prevalence, adjusted by the PsA proportion among psoriasis patients in South America (21.5%) and SUS coverage (71%). For each federative unit, we estimated the number of treated patients (PT), the PT/PAT_ SUS ratio, drug consumption in defined daily doses (DDD), and mean per capita expenditure. Socioeconomic inequalities were measured using the Slope Index of Inequality (SII) and Relative Index of Inequality (RII), with the Human Development Index (HDI) as socioeconomic proxy. Population-weighted regressions were performed, with sensitivity analyses using log-transformed outcomes. Of an estimated 126,587 eligible individuals, 21,731 patient-equivalents received treatment based on DDD-derived APAC records, corresponding to a national coverage rate of 17%. PT/PAT_ SUS ranged from 0.02 to 0.37 (20-fold), per capita expenditure from USD 480 to USD 34,184 (71-fold), and DDD consumption from 2.4 to 78.8 per patient (33-fold). Statistically significant pro-rich gradients were identified for coverage (SII = 0.167; 95%CI: 0.053-0.280; RII = 5.304; 95%CI: 2.373-11.855) and consumption (SII = 48.065; 95%CI: 27.381-68.749; RII = 9.404; 95%CI: 4.550-19.439), with states at the upper socioeconomic extreme showing approximately four- and nine-fold higher values, respectively. Expenditure showed no significant gradient (RII = 0.986; 95%CI: 0.404-2.406). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the direction of all effects, with no gradient inversion. PsA treatment coverage within SUS is markedly low and unevenly distributed across federative units, with statistically significant pro-rich gradients for coverage and consumption but no consistent pattern for expenditure, a finding consistent with territorial misallocation of resources and inequitable distribution of health benefits. Reducing these inequalities requires strengthening diagnostic and care capacity in lower-HDI states alongside systematic equity monitoring within the specialized pharmaceutical care component.

items.title: Atypical predominant thoracic involvement in IgG4-related disease mimicking lung cancer and sarcoidosis: a case report.
items.abstract: To report a rare case of IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) with atypical predominant thoracic involvement mimicking lung cancer and sarcoidosis. A 74-year-old male with a history of heavy smoking presented with chronic cough and exertional dyspnea for 1 year. Chest high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) revealed bronchovascular bundle thickening, a right parahilar mass, multiple perilymphatically distributed solid nodules, lymphadenopathy, and pleural effusion. Laboratory tests revealed marked elevations of serum IgG4 (6710 mg/dL) and IgE (2210 mg/dL). Histopathological examination of lung, pleural biopsy, and lymph node consistently demonstrated dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltration with abundant IgG4-positive plasma cells, without storiform fibrosis or obliterative phlebitis. The patient was definitively diagnosed with IgG4-RD via multidisciplinary team (MDT) consultation. Oral prednisone resulted in significant radiological improvement. IgG4-RD can mimic common thoracic disorders such as lung cancer and sarcoidosis. Early corticosteroid therapy is effective. An experienced MDT, integrating detailed clinical findings, serology, radiology, and histopathology, is essential for prompt diagnosis and timely intervention.
